title: BitCadence Bug & Usability Anomaly Inventory
text:
BitCadence Bug & Usability Anomaly Inventory
Five observations from the hands-on review. Each lists the evidence type: **source** means confirmed by reading the cited code on `main` at the time of writing; **UI** means observed in the running console but not re-verified in a test. An earlier draft listed two more items (a persistent invisible backdrop after backdrop-click, and an invalid `"\B"` escape warning). Neither could be reproduced or located in source, so both were removed.

title: Bug 1: New Job modal does not close on Escape
text:
Bug 1: New Job modal does not close on Escape
**Severity:** Low
**Evidence:** source
**Surface:** Web Console, Job Board
**Component:** `src/mco/console_src/5adac14f-6645-4e02-866b-22c4e571989b.js` (`NewJobForm`, opened by the **+ New job** button)
**Finding:** Clicking the backdrop or the `×` button closes the drawer. No `keydown` / `Escape` handler exists anywhere in `src/mco/console_src`, so pressing Escape does nothing.
**Reproduce:** Open `/console`, Job Board, **+ New job**, press `Escape`. The form stays open.
**Expected:** Escape dismisses the modal, as most users assume.

title: Bug 2: "Register agent" button is hidden in Demo Mode
text:
Bug 2: "Register agent" button is hidden in Demo Mode
**Severity:** Medium
**Evidence:** source
**Surface:** Web Console, Agent Fleet
**Component:** `src/mco/console_src/2ed3f6b1-e1c6-43fc-8b29-31917195cbd5.js:215`
**Code:**
{live ? (
  <Btn kind="primary" small onClick={() => setShowRegister((v) => !v)}>
    {showRegister ? "Cancel" : (tone === "plain" ? "Add agent" : "Register agent")}
  </Btn>
) : null}

**Reproduce:** Open `/console` without connecting a live token, go to **Agent Fleet**.
**Finding:** With `live` false the button renders nothing, so a first-time user sees no graphical way to register an agent and no hint that connecting is required.
**Expected:** A disabled button or a short note explaining that registration needs a live connection.

title: Bug 3: Start BitCadence.bat opens the browser even if the server failed to start
text:
Bug 3: `Start BitCadence.bat` opens the browser even if the server failed to start
**Severity:** Medium
**Evidence:** source
**Surface:** `Start BitCadence.bat:77-79`
**Code:**
start "" /b cmd /c "timeout /t 5 /nobreak >nul & start http://127.0.0.1:18789/console"
".venv\Scripts\python.exe" -m mco.cli serve

**Reproduce:** Make `mco serve` exit immediately (for example, occupy port 18789 first), then run the script.
**Finding:** The browser launch is an unconditional five-second timer. If the server has already exited, the browser opens onto a connection-refused page.
**Expected:** Probe the port (or `/readyz`) before launching the browser.

title: Bug 4: Desktop Manager creates its Tk root without a guard
text:
Bug 4: Desktop Manager creates its Tk root without a guard
**Severity:** Medium
**Evidence:** source (crash not exercised in a headless session)
**Surface:** `src/mco/desktop/app.py`, `DesktopApp.__init__`
**Finding:** `self.root = tk.Tk()` is called with no `try/except`. On a host with no display, `tk.Tk()` raises `TclError`, which would surface as an unhandled traceback rather than a message pointing at `mco status`.
**Reproduce:** Run `python -m mco.desktop.app` from an SSH session or other host with no desktop display.
**Expected:** Catch the error, print a one-line explanation, and exit non-zero.

title: Bug 5: Two flow builders do not share a draft
text:
Bug 5: Two flow builders do not share a draft
**Severity:** Medium
**Evidence:** source and UI
**Surface:** `/console` Workflows tab versus `/flow` Design mode
**Finding:** `/flow` is a standalone page (`src/mco/static/flow.html`) and the console builder is part of the console bundle. A search of both for draft persistence found no shared storage; the only `localStorage` key used by `flow.html` is the access token. A workflow drawn in one builder does not appear in the other, except through YAML export and import.
**Reproduce:** Build a three-step workflow in the console Workflows tab, then open `/flow` and choose **Design workflow**. The canvas is empty.
**Expected:** One shared draft, or a single builder.

title: BitCadence Friction Inventory & Flow Surfaces Audit

**Historical audit.** This was written against the console before the v0.6.0 redesign. The `img/` names below refer to screenshots that were replaced or removed (the workflow builder, Flow Control and agent fleet screens no longer exist). Helpers, Ask and Connect an AI replaced them.
BitCadence Friction Inventory & Flow Surfaces Audit
This document presents a comprehensive, hands-on audit of user friction across every user-facing surface of BitCadence, evaluated against two non-technical personas:
**Persona A (Gen-X / Older Adult):** An intelligent professional who was not raised on computers, feels intimidated by terminals, command prompts, environment variables, and cryptic error messages, and expects clear visual guidance.
**Persona B (Smartphone-Native Teen):** A user raised entirely on iOS/Android who expects 1-tap actions, zero configuration, no manual copying of ports or URLs, and instant visual gratification.

title: Critical Friction Analysis: Elevation & Terminal Barriers
page: BitCadence Friction Inventory & Flow Surfaces Audit
text:
Critical Friction Analysis: Elevation & Terminal Barriers
A focused audit of sidecar management and desktop operations reveals a severe divide between the GUI vision and operational reality:
1. Tasks Blocked by "Run as Administrator" (UAC Elevation)
**Installing Unattended Sidecars (`background = true` / S4U Logon):** Windows Task Scheduler refuses to register S4U logon tasks from unattended or standard user shells without Administrator elevation (`Access is denied`).
**Local Service Accounts & ACL Hardening (`admin-pack.ps1`):** Creating dedicated service accounts and locking them out of private directories (`%USERPROFILE%`, personal documents, SSH keys) requires full local Administrator rights.
**Port Narrowing & Firewall Rules:** Narrowing inbound ports to localhost (`127.0.0.1`) requires elevated PowerShell.
**Impact on Personas:**
**Persona A (Older Adult):** Freezes at Windows UAC prompts. Cannot locate "Run as administrator" in the Start Menu and assumes system warnings indicate dangerous activity.
**Persona B (Teen):** Has never encountered an administrative prompt or terminal on mobile devices. Assumes the software is fundamentally broken when permission errors occur.
2. Tasks Forcing Users into a Terminal / PowerShell
**Desktop Shortcut & Dependency Setup:** `install_desktop.ps1` requires running a command line with explicit `-Python` paths.
**Autostart at Sign-in:** `desktop_autostart.ps1` requires passing `-Pythonw "C:\path\to\pythonw.exe"`. Neither persona knows where their virtual environment's `pythonw.exe` binary resides.
**Fleet Reconciliation (`fleet.toml`):** Changing worker allocation requires editing TOML syntax in Notepad and running `mco fleet apply`.
**Silent Failure Diagnostics (Locked Logs & Duplicate Wakers):** When a worker appears "online" but fails silently, diagnosing locked files (`~/.mco/logs/<instance>.log`) or detecting duplicate wakers requires complex PowerShell commands (`Get-Process`, `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, `schtasks /query`).

title: 1. Inventory of Flow Surfaces in BitCadence
page: BitCadence Friction Inventory & Flow Surfaces Audit
text:
1. Inventory of Flow Surfaces in BitCadence
The audit identified **five distinct surfaces** where workflows, execution flows, or Scores are displayed or authored:
**Overview Dashboard Stepper (`WorkflowStrip`):**
**Location:** `http://127.0.0.1:18789/console` (Overview tab).
**User Capabilities:** Read-only inspection. Groups active jobs by `workflow` name and renders a horizontal linear stepper showing step completion and current running task.
**Interaction:** Clicking any step opens the Job Detail Drawer. Cannot edit, re-order, or add steps.
**Console Workflow Builder (`WorkflowBuilder`):**
**Location:** `http://127.0.0.1:18789/console` (Workflows tab).
**User Capabilities:** Authoring and submitting DAGs. Users can add step cards, edit step IDs, select target roles, type prompt instructions, toggle approval gates, and export/import YAML.
**Interaction:** Visual card graph. Step connections can be added. Submits directly via `POST /api/workflows`.
**Flow Control Live Board (`/flow`):**
**Location:** `http://127.0.0.1:18789/flow` (Live board mode).
**User Capabilities:** Real-time operational mimic. Renders every job on the board with true `depends_on` arrows, animated dashed lines for active data flows, and color-coded status badges.
**Interaction:** Clicking nodes opens a side inspector where operators can directly click **Approve**, **Reject**, **Retry**, or **Cancel**. Strictly read-only for layout; graph structure is driven 100% by live database state.
**Flow Control Design Mode (`/flow`):**
**Location:** `http://127.0.0.1:18789/flow` (Design workflow mode).
**User Capabilities:** Visual CAD/drafting canvas. Features a grid canvas, step stencil rail, drag-to-place cards, and interactive circular port connectors (`then` → `needs`).
**Interaction:** Authoring only. Features local DAG validation, cycle detection, YAML export, and a separate red **Run workflow** confirmation button.
**Autonomous Score Conductor (`AutonomyLiveLookModal` & CLI):**
**Location:** `http://127.0.0.1:18789/console` (Live look modal) and `mco score`.
**User Capabilities:** Monitoring long-running autonomous Score contracts. Shows active goal stages, target agents, progress percentage, and lease status.
**Interaction:** Offline CLI compiles and validates JSON contracts. Conductor advances runs automatically based on evidence receipts.

title: 2. Does an Editable Flow Builder Make Sense?
page: BitCadence Friction Inventory & Flow Surfaces Audit
text:
2. Does an Editable Flow Builder Make Sense?
The Verdict: **Partially Yes, but the Current Mental Model is Inverted**
**Why it makes sense:**
**Visual Interlock Verification:** For enterprise operators, compliance auditors, and safety engineers, visually seeing the dependency chain and where the human approval gate sits is irreplaceable. A flowchart is self-documenting in a way raw YAML or JSON never is.
**Live Progress Visualization:** Flow Control (`/flow`) with its animated flowing edges is an outstanding operational tool. It immediately communicates bottlenecks (e.g., three tasks blocked waiting for a slow build step).
**Why an editable drag-and-drop canvas has severe friction:**
**The "Blank Canvas Problem":** Asking a user to drag boxes, invent IDs like `step-1`, memorize model roles, and drag crosshair wires between ports is 1990s CAD software UX. Modern users (especially mobile-native teens and busy managers) do not want to wire boxes.
**Duplication & Confusion:** Having two separate builders (`/console#workflows` vs `/flow#design`) creates confusion. They share the same underlying YAML schema but use completely different UIs.
**Recommendation for Redesign:**
**Merge the surfaces:** Keep `/flow` as the single canonical Flow Control surface.
**Conversational Prompt-to-Flow:** Replace manual box-dragging with a natural-language flow generator powered by Jev:
*"User types: 'Research open PRs, run tests, and if green, draft release notes and ask me to publish.' -> Jev automatically compiles the 4-step DAG with the approval gate pre-configured."*
The visual canvas should be used for **reviewing and tweaking**, not building from scratch.

title: 3. Score Data Available to Auto-Generate a Live Flowchart
page: BitCadence Friction Inventory & Flow Surfaces Audit
text:
3. Score Data Available to Auto-Generate a Live Flowchart
Score state is split between the immutable score document and the run's execution tables. Column names below are from `src/mco/migrations/2026-09_score_store.sql` (Postgres) and the task shape validated in `src/mco/orchestrator/scores.py`. The local SQLite conductor (`~/.mco/score-runs.db`) keeps the same concepts but is a separate store; check its schema before binding a UI to it.
Data Element
Where it actually lives
Representation in a Live Flowchart
**Nodes (Tasks / Goals)**
`score_documents.document` (JSONB): `tasks[]` with `id`, `goal`, `title`, `role`; run-time rows in `score_tasks` (`run_id`, `task_id`, `attempt`)
Node cards labeled with task id and title
**Dependencies**
`depends_on` list on each task inside `score_documents.document`. It is **not** a `score_tasks` column.
Directed arrows from prerequisite to dependent
**Execution States**
`score_tasks.status`. Statuses seen in the conductor code include `running`, `review`, `accepted`; the full set is defined in `scores.py`, not in the migration.
Status coloring, mapped from whatever values the conductor emits
**Resource Locks**
`resources` list on each task inside the score document. Tasks that share a resource are serialized by the conductor; there is no lock column.
Badge on nodes that share a resource lane
**Assigned Workers**
`score_tasks.author_id` and `score_tasks.author_provider`; reviewers in `score_reviews.reviewer_id`; catalog in `score_providers`
Worker chip on the active node
**Budget**
`score_runs.authorized_budget_cents`, `score_grants.budget_cents`; per-task `max_cost_cents` in the document
Run-level cost meter
**Human Checkpoints**
`checkpoint` flag on the task inside the document; approval recorded in `score_tasks.checkpoint_approved` (boolean)
Shield icon or pause barrier on the node
**History**
`score_events` (append-only: `seq`, `run_id`, `kind`, `task_id`, `at`, `actor`, `payload`)
Timeline or replay

title: 4. APIs & Events Available for Live Updates
page: BitCadence Friction Inventory & Flow Surfaces Audit
text:
4. APIs & Events Available for Live Updates
Verified against the gateway routes in `src/mco/cli.py`, `src/mco/orchestrator/routes.py` and `score_gate_routes.py`:
**WebSocket Broadcast Feed (`/ws/broadcast`):**
The gateway pushes one frame per job event. The envelope is `type` plus a nested `payload`, which carries the event name and the full job row:
{
  "type": "event",
  "payload": {
    "event": "status:completed",
    "job": { "id": "88f57ed8-4069-...", "status": "completed" }
  }
}

Frames are filtered per connection: non-admin identities only receive jobs addressed to their own role or instance. No latency figure has been measured, so none is claimed here.
**Job Event Stream API (`GET /api/jobs/{id}/events`):**
Returns the tamper-evident event log for one job.
**Project view (`GET /api/jobs/project-view`):**
Grouped job data that the Projects dashboard polls.
**Score gates and grants (`/api/score/gates`, `/api/score/grants`):**
These are the only Score HTTP routes in the gateway today. They expose human gates and grants, not run or task state.
**No Score run or event routes yet:**
There is no `GET /api/scores/runs/{run_id}` and no `GET /api/scores/{digest}/events`. A live Score flowchart would need new read-only routes over `score_runs`, `score_tasks` and `score_events`, or it can read run state through `mco score status --run-id <run-id>` on the conductor host.
**Polling Fallback:**
If WebSocket is blocked by a corporate proxy, poll `GET /api/jobs` or `GET /api/jobs/project-view` on a short interval.

title: Helpers & Presence
text: Helpers & Presence

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Add a helper, see at a glance which helpers are working, ready or stuck, and rotate a helper's access token. A helper is one AI worker that takes jobs from the board. (The command line still calls them agents, for example `mco agents`.)

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. See your helpers
text:
1. See your helpers
In the left menu, click **Helpers**.
![Your helpers](img/08-console-helpers.png)
Each helper has a card with a friendly name, a light and a word:
**Working** (green): it holds a job right now, and the card says which one.
**Ready** (green): it is waiting for a job.
**Stuck**: it needs a fix. Click **Fix it** on the card. BitCadence shows what it will do and asks before it does anything.
**Not connected** (grey): it has not been heard from.
Each card also says when the helper was last heard from. See [Helpers](Helpers.md) for how the lights are decided.

title: 2. Add a helper
text:
2. Add a helper
Click **+ Add a helper**.
![Add a helper](img/17-helper-add-panel.png)
Pick which AI should power it and give it a name, for example *Penny*.
Click **Add helper**. BitCadence registers it and saves its sign-in on this computer. The page says "Penny is added" and never shows the sign-in. An existing helper's name is refused instead of silently replacing its sign-in.
To link Claude, Codex, Gemini, Antigravity or Cursor in one tap instead, use [Connect an AI](Connect-an-AI.md).

title: 3. Rotate a helper's access token
text:
3. Rotate a helper's access token
If a credential is lost or exposed, run `mco reset-token <name>` (see below). A new token is minted and the old one stops working at once.

title: 4. Remove a stale helper
text:
4. Remove a stale helper
Run `mco deregister <name>` to remove its registration.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
# List all registered helpers and presence
mco agents

# Register a new helper
mco register --name worker-east-1 --role codex

# Register a helper with restricted scopes
mco register --name monitor-1 --role viewer --scope jobs:read

# Rotate a helper's access token
mco reset-token worker-east-1

# Deregister a helper
mco deregister worker-east-1

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Presence Heartbeats:** When a helper runs `mco listen` or queries `mco_inbox`, its `last_seen_at` timestamp updates automatically.
**Safe Concurrency:** Two helpers with the same role share the role's inbox. When work arrives, whichever helper requests a lease first wins atomically. The other helper receives an empty response and continues waiting.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Helper shows Not connected despite running"
text:
1. "Helper shows Not connected despite running"
**Cause:** Network connectivity lost, or worker polling loop was stopped.
**Fix:** A helper is considered offline if no heartbeat occurs within 90 seconds. Restart the worker process or verify network reachability to the gateway.

title: 2. "Token lost after registration"
text:
2. "Token lost after registration"
**Cause:** The panel was closed before copying the token.
**Fix:** Run `mco reset-token <name>` to generate a new token.

title: 3. "Cannot delete helper: jobs currently leased"
text:
3. "Cannot delete helper: jobs currently leased"
**Cause:** The helper is actively holding an open lease on an unfinished job.
**Fix:** Wait for the job to complete, or use `mco cancel <job-id>` to cancel the leased job before deleting the helper.

title: Approvals & Governance
text: Approvals & Governance

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Implement human-in-the-loop oversight, authorize or reject high-risk helper operations at safety gates, trigger the emergency kill switch, and export tamper-evident audit evidence packs.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Open Approvals
text:
1. Open Approvals
Click **Approvals** in the left menu. The badge next to it shows how many jobs are paused at an approval gate.
![Needs your OK](img/05-console-approvals.png)

title: 2. Review a paused job
text:
2. Review a paused job
Pick a job from the list on the left. The panel on the right shows:
**Title and description:** what the helper wants to do.
**Will run on:** which helper role would do the work if you say yes.
**Requested by:** who asked for it.
**Full details:** opens the job with its history.

title: 3. Make a decision
text:
3. Make a decision
**To say yes:** click **Approve & run**. The job moves from `needs_approval` to `pending`, a helper can pick it up, and the audit log records who approved it.
**To say no:** type a reason in **Reason for saying no** and click **Reject**. The job becomes `rejected` and no helper will touch it.
To handle several at once, tick their boxes or use **Select all**.
The same **Approve** button also appears on **Home** under **What needs you**. See [Approvals](Approvals.md) for how the console checks that you are allowed to approve.

title: 4. Pause everything (kill switch)
text:
4. Pause everything (kill switch)
When something unexpected is happening:
Click **Settings**, and in the **Pause everything** card click **Pause**.
Helpers stop taking new work and no new jobs are started.
Jobs already in progress finish; you can still look, approve and reject.
Click **Resume** on the same card to start again.
See [Settings](Settings.md). The `MCO_KILL_SWITCH` setting is the same switch.

title: 5. Governance page and evidence export
text:
5. Governance page and evidence export
Click **Governance** for the pending approvals, the decision history and the oversight trail in one place.
![Governance](img/06-console-governance.png)
To export evidence, pick a **Start** and **End** date and click **Export compliance evidence pack**. You get a PDF cover page plus a JSON audit trail for EU AI Act Art. 12 record-keeping and Art. 14 human oversight.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
# Approve a job at the human gate
mco approve <job-id>

# Reject a job with recorded rationale
mco reject <job-id> --reason "Production deployment window closed"

# View tamper-evident event history
mco audit <job-id>

# Export a signed cryptographic audit checkpoint
mco audit-checkpoint <job-id> checkpoint.json

# Enable emergency kill switch from terminal
mco settings MCO_KILL_SWITCH true
mco restart

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Immutable History:** In the database (`agent_job_events`), every approval decision is written to an append-only table. Any database `UPDATE` or `DELETE` query on this table is rejected at the storage engine level.
**Audit Receipt:** In the job's details, the history explicitly stamps:
approved · actor: local-operator (role: admin) · 2026-10-03 12:25:00 UTC

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "403 Forbidden: Approver role required"
text:
1. "403 Forbidden: Approver role required"
**Cause:** The bearer token used to approve the job belongs to a role that is not listed in `MCO_APPROVER_ROLES`.
**Fix:** By default, approver roles are `human,admin,operator`. Re-authenticate with an admin or human token, or configure:
mco settings MCO_APPROVER_ROLES "human,admin,operator,reviewer"

title: 2. "Kill switch active: Cannot lease task"
text:
2. "Kill switch active: Cannot lease task"
**Cause:** The kill switch was left enabled (`MCO_KILL_SWITCH=true`).
**Fix:** On **Settings**, click **Resume** in the **Pause everything** card, or run:
mco settings MCO_KILL_SWITCH false

title: Approvals
text:
Approvals
Open `/console` and choose **Approvals** ("Needs your OK"), or run `bitcadence
approve`. Nothing sensitive happens until you say so.

title: When you can't approve yet
text:
When you can't approve yet
A missing approver right used to show up as `403 Forbidden: missing scope
jobs:approve`. It no longer does. In a terminal:
$ bitcadence approve
You can't approve yet because your account isn't an approver.
Fix it? [Y/n] y
Done. You can approve now.
Approved: Publish release notes.

Enter or `Y` makes the account on this computer an approver and then approves.
`N` changes nothing and points to `bitcadence fix`. `bitcadence fix` finds the same
problem on its own and offers the same repair. With no terminal and no `--yes`,
the right is never granted.
The repair edits this computer's own account, from a terminal you are sitting at.
It works only on the built-in local database; if your account is managed
somewhere else you are told to ask the person who runs BitCadence. There is
deliberately no web or API button for it, because an account that cannot approve
must not be able to promote itself over the network.
In the console, a refused Approve/Reject shows a card in words ("You can't approve
this yet. Your account isn't set up as an approver", with the command to run)
instead of an HTTP error.

title: Approved, but nobody is free
text:
Approved, but nobody is free
If no helper is online for the job, you are told so and pointed to `bitcadence
helpers add`. See [Helpers](Helpers.md).

title: Ask for something
text:
Ask for something
Open `/console` and choose **Ask for something**, or run `bitcadence ask` in a
terminal. Both use the same planner: say what you want in plain words, check the
drawn plan, and approve once.

title: In the console
text:
In the console
Type what should happen, for example: *Research open PRs, run tests, if green
draft release notes and ask me to publish.* Two example buttons fill the box
for you.
**Draft a plan** draws the steps in order. "If everything passes" appears
between steps that only run after a check. A dashed step marked "you decide"
is a point where it stops and asks you.
Make only light tweaks:
**Remove a step** shows a Remove button on each step. A plan always keeps at
least one step.
**Always ask me at the end** adds a final "Ask you before finishing" step.
**Make it repeat** offers every day, every weekday or every Friday at 9 AM.
The plan then also shows up under Schedules.
**Approve and start** creates the work. Your Approve click is the OK, so only
the plan's own "ask you" steps wait for you again. **Change my request** goes
back to the text box; to change the plan itself, edit the request and draft
again.
Nothing is created until you approve. If you are not connected yet (demo mode),
the page asks you to connect first.

title: In a terminal
text:
In a terminal
bitcadence ask "tidy the install docs"
bitcadence ask "Research open PRs, run tests, if green draft release notes and ask me to publish."
bitcadence ask "tidy the install docs" --remove 2 --ask-me --repeat "every Friday at 9 AM"

The plan prints as a numbered list and asks `Start this? [Y/n]`. `--remove N`
leaves out step N (repeat it for more), `--ask-me` always asks at the end,
`--repeat` makes it repeat, and `--yes` skips the question. From a terminal the
first step also waits for `bitcadence approve`.

title: Workflow files
text:
Workflow files
The drag-and-drop workflow builders are gone from the console. Workflow YAML
files still work and run exactly as before:
bitcadence ask --file plan.yaml
mco workflow plan.yaml

A repeat saves the plan as `~/.mco/workflows/ask-<name>.yaml` and adds a
schedule to `~/.mco/schedules.yaml` (the old file is kept as
`schedules.yaml.bak`). The older `mco gui --flow` option still works and opens
the console.

title: How the plan is drawn
text:
How the plan is drawn
Commas, "then" and "ask me ..." split the request into steps, one per clause.
"If green" or "if it passes" becomes a condition on the next step. This is a
simple, predictable reading of your sentence, not a guess about what you meant:
if the drawn plan is wrong, reword the request and draft again.

title: Connect an AI
text:
Connect an AI
Open `/console` and choose **Connect an AI**, or run `bitcadence connect` in a
terminal. Both do the same thing: find the app on this computer and add
BitCadence to its connection settings. You never edit a file.
![Connect an AI](img/22-console-connect-ai.png)
The screenshot is from a computer with none of these apps installed, so every card says **Not found**. On your computer, a card for an app that is installed has a **Connect** button you can tap.
$ bitcadence connect claude
I'll add BitCadence to Claude's settings (a backup is kept).
Go ahead? [Y/n]
Connected. Restart Claude to see it.

title: Apps
text:
Apps
Say
App
`claude`
Claude (chat and desktop app)
`codex`
ChatGPT / Codex
`gemini`
Gemini
`antigravity`
Antigravity
`cursor`
Cursor
`other`
Any other app: shows a code you can copy
`bitcadence connect` alone shows a pick list. In the console each app has one
**Connect** button, a **Connected** / **Not connected** / **Not found** word with
a shape (never colour alone), and, once connected, **Send a test** and
**Disconnect**.

title: Safe by design
text:
Safe by design
The original settings file is copied to a `.bak` first. The first backup is
never overwritten, so repeating connect and disconnect keeps your original.
A settings file we can't read is left alone, with a plain message.
Other servers and settings in the file are kept as they were.
Connecting twice changes nothing. `bitcadence connect claude --disconnect`
removes only BitCadence.
`bitcadence connect claude --test` (or **Send a test**) checks that the setting
is in place and the program it starts exists. Close and reopen the app once.
If the app isn't installed: `I couldn't find Gemini on this computer. Install it,
then run: bitcadence connect gemini`.
The console uses `/api/connect-ai` (list, `/{app}/connect`, `/{app}/disconnect`,
`/{app}/test`). It returns app names and plain sentences only, never a file path
or a sign-in.

title: Connecting the Console & Demo Mode
text: Connecting the Console & Demo Mode

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Connect the BitCadence console to your local gateway using an access token, or use the simulated Demo mode to look around safely before running live tasks.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Open the Web Console
text:
1. Open the Web Console
Open your web browser and navigate to:
http://127.0.0.1:18789/console

When first opened, the console loads in **Demo mode — simulated data**. The bottom of the left menu says **Demo · simulated data**: every job, helper and event shown is a simulation, so you can explore without running real work.

title: 2. Open Connection Settings
text:
2. Open Connection Settings
Click **Settings** in the left menu, then open **Show advanced** at the bottom of the page. The connection form is inside it.
![Console Settings Connection Panel](img/02-console-settings.png)

title: 3. Enter Gateway URL and Access Token
text:
3. Enter Gateway URL and Access Token
In the **Connection** section:
**Gateway URL:** Ensure it is set to `http://127.0.0.1:18789` (already populated by default).
**Agent token:** Paste the operator access token generated during installation (`Ctrl+V`). The token begins with `mco_tok_`.
*Where to find your token:* Look at the server terminal window, or open `~/.mco/.env` in Notepad and copy the value of `MCO_LOCAL_TOKEN`.

title: 4. Click Connect
text:
4. Click Connect
Click the **Connect** button.
The bottom of the left menu changes from **Demo · simulated data** to **Live**, and a toast says your helpers are ready.
The connection parameters are stored safely in your browser's `localStorage` (`bitcadence_conn`), meaning you will not have to re-enter them on subsequent visits.

title: 5. Returning to Demo Mode (Optional)
text:
5. Returning to Demo Mode (Optional)
If you ever want to return to sandbox exploration with mock data:
In **Settings → Show advanced → Connection**, click **Disconnect**.
The UI instantly reverts to simulated state, allowing you to click all controls safely.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
To verify connectivity and token authorization directly from your shell:
# Set token in environment
$env:MCO_AGENT_TOKEN = (Get-Content "$HOME\.mco\.env" | Select-String "MCO_LOCAL_TOKEN").Line.Split("=")[1]
$env:MCO_GATEWAY_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:18789"

# Test health check and auth
mco status

# List online helpers
mco agents

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Header Status:** The top right shows a glowing green indicator stating:
Live • 127.0.0.1:18789 • local-operator (admin)

**Real Data Sync:** The Job Board, Portfolio and Helpers pages now display the actual rows from your local SQLite database (`~/.mco/local.db`).
**Live WebSocket:** A real-time WebSocket connection is established to `/ws/broadcast`. Any job created by CLI or another helper immediately animates onto your screen without refreshing.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "401 Unauthorized" or "Invalid token"
text:
1. "401 Unauthorized" or "Invalid token"
**Cause:** Incomplete token pasted or mismatched local token.
**Fix:** Copy the exact token from `~/.mco/.env`. Verify that there are no leading or trailing whitespace characters. Tokens always start with `mco_tok_`.

title: 2. "Network Error: Failed to fetch"
text:
2. "Network Error: Failed to fetch"
**Cause:** The BitCadence gateway server is stopped or running on a different port.
**Fix:** Start the server using `Start BitCadence.bat` or `mco serve`. Confirm that `http://127.0.0.1:18789/healthz` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

title: 3. "Console reverts to Demo mode after page reload"
text:
3. "Console reverts to Demo mode after page reload"
**Cause:** Browser privacy settings or an incognito window blocked `localStorage`.
**Fix:** Ensure cookies and local site storage are allowed for `127.0.0.1`. If using Private Browsing, re-enter the token.

title: Console Home
text:
Console Home
Open `/console` and choose **Home**. **What needs you** comes first: approval
requests, unsuccessful work, and active jobs with no sign of life. **Approve**
uses the existing authenticated approval action; **Look first** opens the job
details. Job identifiers are absent from Home cards.
**What's running** groups Score jobs by their run, so two runs of the same plan
remain separate. Cards show a state word and a sentence from worker progress,
with a plain fallback when no progress sentence is available. Structured output
and recognizable credential text are not used as progress sentences.
Step counts come from the actual Score plan, not a count of recently fetched
jobs; repeat rounds are labelled. Home refreshes at most twenty visible plans
every thirty seconds. If a plan cannot be read, its card omits the step count.
Tap a Score card to watch its read-only live drawing. Other cards open job
details. Home polls `/api/jobs?limit=200` and `/api/agents`; it never requests an
unbounded job board. A notice appears at the 200-job limit because older work
may be outside this view. This is a recent-work view, not a complete history.
The named `HOME_STALL_MINUTES` setting in the console source is **10**. For
leased or working jobs, the newest valid start, update, progress timestamp or
worker heartbeat starts the silence clock. Waiting and approval jobs are not
flagged merely because they are old. Missing timestamps do not prove a stall.
The **Stuck** label is a display flag; viewing it never changes the job or
restarts a helper. Check the job details before choosing a repair.
Cards use words as well as color, visible keyboard focus, and controls at least
48 pixels high. The view follows light/dark preferences and reduced motion.
See [Live Score](Score-live.md) for the automatic drawing and its limits.

title: Coverage and verification
text:
Coverage and verification
This wiki was checked against the BitCadence source snapshot on **November 13, 2026**. It separates everyday walkthroughs from exact references, and shipped routes from proposed designs.

title: CLI coverage
text:
CLI coverage
The [complete CLI reference](mco-cli-reference.md) maps **93 command/group paths** and **301 arguments and options** across the shared `bitcadence` / `mco` tree. It includes nested groups, defaults, required arguments, option aliases, repeatable values, hidden compatibility options and synthesized help/completion options. Each command has a purpose, safe example, expected result and recovery notes.
The [machine-readable inventory](_review/cli-coverage.json) binds every path and parameter to a documentation anchor and source metadata. The checker compares the actual Typer command tree without invoking operational callbacks. Unknown commands/options, changed defaults and missing anchors are failures. Negative-control checks also verified that the checker rejects missing/stale commands and parameters.
The desktop executable is separate and is covered under [Windows Local Control and tray](gui-reference.md#windows-local-control-and-tray).

title: GUI coverage
text:
GUI coverage
The [GUI reference](gui-reference.md) covers the twelve console navigation pages, Score and detail views, the five-page technical dashboard, model-connection/lock/modal flows, Windows manager/tray actions and all **33 server-driven settings**. Its [279 grouped control/workflow mappings](_review/gui-feature-coverage.json) link instructions to source locations.
This is a manually grouped feature inventory, not a claim that every possible dynamic server record or option value was enumerated. Defined-but-unreachable legacy components and pending local changes are explicitly identified; they are not presented as released controls.
Source hashes make interface drift visible. A changed GUI source file requires reviewing/updating the inventory before strict coverage passes again. Hash checks prove the source baseline, not rendered behavior or successful effects.

title: What was checked safely
text:
What was checked safely
Recursive command/parameter coverage, required documentation anchors and parser-valid examples.
Every local documentation link, image and fragment in the generated website.
The help site's section search, keyboard access, copy controls and narrow-screen navigation.
Regression tests for technical-dashboard prompt cancellation: pressing Cancel submits no abort or batch-cancel request; an intentional blank confirmation still follows the supported behavior.
Legacy-domain redirects for both old hostnames, HTTP/HTTPS, root and path/query requests; removal of the obsolete site project.
No real jobs were approved, cancelled, retried, reassigned or published to perform these checks. No live helper was stopped and no production token/configuration was changed. Provider calls and destructive product controls require disposable fixtures or separate operational authorization, not a documentation test against someone's live work.

title: Current limits and known issues
text:
Current limits and known issues
The [usability review](UX-REVIEW.md) contains source-confirmed issues and concrete acceptance checks. Product GUI behavior is source-reviewed; this refresh does not claim that every backend integration was exercised on every operating system. Existing screenshots illustrate the workflow and may precede small label changes.
The Cancel-prompt fix is included in this source branch. An already-running gateway does not acquire a code patch just because the public help site was published. The live product needs its normal reviewed release/update before that fix can be assumed installed.

title: Keep the wiki complete
text:
Keep the wiki complete
From a source checkout, using the project's Python environment:
python docs/wiki/_review/verify_cli_coverage.py --repo .
python docs/wiki/_review/verify_gui_coverage.py --repo . --strict-hashes
python docs/wiki/_review/verify_cli_examples.py docs/wiki
python scripts/build_wiki.py

CI runs the coverage checkers and site build alongside the tests. When a feature changes, update its steps, expected result, failure/recovery guidance and inventory entry, then rebuild. Keep credentials and household/machine-specific data out of public documentation.

title: Desktop Manager, Installer & System Tray
text: Desktop Manager, Installer & System Tray

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Install, launch, operate, update, and troubleshoot the native BitCadence Windows Desktop Manager (`scripts/desktop.pyw`), system tray icon, one-click installer, and background process supervisor without keeping raw terminal windows open.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Installation: One-Click Installer & Desktop Shortcut
text:
1. Installation: One-Click Installer & Desktop Shortcut
BitCadence offers two installation methods on Windows:
Method A: The One-Click Installer (`install.bat` / `scripts/install.ps1`)
For new users and end-user workstations:
Double-click **`install.bat`** in the repository root (or run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1`).
The installer automatically:
Locates or downloads Python 3.9+.
Creates a private virtual environment (`.venv`).
Generates a local access token (`mco_tok_...`) and configuration (`~/.mco/.env`).
Adds `mco` to your User `PATH` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\BitCadence\bin`).
Creates a **BitCadence** shortcut on your Desktop pointing to the launcher.
Method B: Desktop Component Setup (`scripts/install_desktop.ps1`)
For existing source checkouts or developers:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install_desktop.ps1 -Python .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe

This script:
Installs desktop UI dependencies (`pystray`, `Pillow`) into `.codex/desktopdeps`.
Generates the official multi-resolution icon (`.codex/bitcadence.ico`).
Verifies that `pythonw.exe` exists in your Python directory.
Generates standard Windows shortcuts (`BitCadence.lnk`) in both your **Desktop** and **Start Menu Programs** folders pointing to:
Target: <path-to>\pythonw.exe "<repo-root>\scripts\desktop.pyw"
Start In: <repo-root>

title: 2. First Launch & Guided Startup
text:
2. First Launch & Guided Startup
Double-click the **BitCadence** icon on your Desktop or Start menu.
![BitCadence Desktop Control Window](img/19-desktop-control-window.png)
What Happens on First Launch:
**Window-Free Launch:** Launched via `pythonw.exe`, so no black command prompt window flashes or remains on your screen.
**Single-Instance Guard:** If BitCadence is already running, launching the shortcut again does not start a duplicate server. Instead, it signals the existing instance via `~/.mco/desktop/show-window` and brings the existing window to the front.
**Automatic Component Discovery:** The app inspects your system to identify running gateways, schedulers, and workers.
**Clicking "Start All":**
Starts the Gateway API server (`http://127.0.0.1:18789`).
Waits for the `/readyz` health probe to pass (up to 30 seconds).
Starts the background Scheduler daemon.
Starts all configured workers in `~/.mco/fleet.toml` whose mode is set to `waker` or `poll`.

title: 3. What Starts Automatically
text:
3. What Starts Automatically
When you click **Start all** (or launch with `--start-all`), the supervisor starts the complete local stack in strict topological order:
Component
Command Invoked
Purpose
**Gateway Server**
`python.exe -m mco.cli serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18789`
Local API server, SQLite database interface, SSE event bus, and Web Console backend.
**Scheduler**
`python.exe -m mco.cli schedule run`
Evaluates cron loops and interval automation declared in `~/.mco/schedules.yaml`.
**Fleet Workers**
Commands configured in `~/.mco/fleet.toml`
Starts event wakers or polling processes for each active agent (e.g., `codex-beast`, `claude-cio`).
**Process Guard (Windows Job Object):** All child processes spawned by the supervisor are attached to a Windows Job Object configured with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`. If the desktop supervisor terminates unexpectedly or crashes, the Windows kernel automatically terminates all child worker processes, preventing orphaned background zombies.

title: 4. System Tray & Minimized Behavior
text:
4. System Tray & Minimized Behavior
The Desktop Manager integrates with the Windows Notification Area (System Tray):
**Minimizing to Tray on Close (X):** Clicking the **X** button in the window title bar does **not** terminate BitCadence. It withdraws the window into the notification tray, keeping all background agents and the gateway running uninterrupted.
**Starting Minimized at Boot:** Running with the `--minimized` flag starts the application directly in the notification tray without ever flashing a GUI window:
pythonw.exe scripts\desktop.pyw --start-all --minimized

**System Tray Context Menu:** Right-clicking the BitCadence tray icon provides:
**Open BitCadence:** Restores the main Control window.
**Start all:** Starts all configured stack components.
**Stop all:** Gracefully stops workers, scheduler, and gateway.
**Open console:** Launches your default web browser directly to `http://127.0.0.1:18789/console`.
**Exit:** Gracefully terminates all supervisor-owned child processes and exits the application completely.

title: 5. Configuring Autostart on Sign-in
text:
5. Configuring Autostart on Sign-in
To have BitCadence automatically start in the tray whenever you log in to Windows:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\desktop_autostart.ps1 -Pythonw "C:\path\to\.venv\Scripts\pythonw.exe"

This places a shortcut in `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup` configured with `--start-all --minimized`.
To remove autostart:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\desktop_autostart.ps1 -Remove

title: 6. Where the Logs Live
text:
6. Where the Logs Live
BitCadence organizes logs cleanly on disk:
Log File
Path
What It Contains
**Desktop Supervisor**
`~/.mco/desktop/logs/desktop.log`
Supervisor lifecycle events, start/stop requests, and process health checks.
**Component Logs**
`~/.mco/desktop/logs/<component>.log`
Combined stdout/stderr for each individual managed component (`gateway.log`, `scheduler.log`, `<instance>.log`).
**Standalone Gateway**
`~/.mco/logs/gateway.log`
Gateway server logs when run outside the desktop supervisor.
**Individual Agent Logs**
`~/.mco/logs/<instance>.log`
Output generated by worker CLI executors.
Filtering Logs in the GUI:
In the Desktop Control window:
Click any row in the **Component table** (e.g., `gateway` or `claude-cio`).
The bottom log viewer instantly filters to show the last 100 lines of output for that selected component.
Deselecting rows returns to the unified log stream.

title: 7. Updating BitCadence
text:
7. Updating BitCadence
Updating Source Installations:
The setup script includes automated upstream update checks:
Open PowerShell in the BitCadence directory:
git pull --ff-only origin main

In the Desktop Control window, click **Reload settings** to pick up configuration changes, or click **Restart all** to restart services with updated code.
Updating Package Installations:
If installed via pip:
pip install --upgrade "bitcadence[desktop]"

title: 8. Uninstalling
text:
8. Uninstalling
To cleanly remove BitCadence from your computer:
**Exit the Desktop Manager:** Right-click the system tray icon and select **Exit** (or run `python -m mco.desktop.app --quit`).
**Remove Autostart:**
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\desktop_autostart.ps1 -Remove

**Remove Shortcuts:** Delete `BitCadence.lnk` from your Desktop and Start Menu Programs folders.
**Clean up Configuration & Logs:** Delete the `~/.mco` directory (`Remove-Item -Recurse ~/.mco`).
**Delete Repository / Environment:** Delete the BitCadence installation folder.

text:
Linux Alternative:
On Linux, the Desktop GUI is deliberately disabled (`if os.name != "nt": raise SystemExit("The desktop manager currently supports Windows.")`). Instead, Linux operators use native `systemd` user units:
mco service install

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "SupervisorAlreadyRunning" Error on Startup
text:
1. "SupervisorAlreadyRunning" Error on Startup
**Cause:** Another instance of `desktop.pyw` is already running or held open in the system tray.
**Fix:** Check your system tray (notification area overflow arrow). If present, right-click and choose **Open BitCadence**. If stuck, terminate lingering Python processes:
python -m mco.desktop.app --quit

title: 2. "Pillow or pystray not found"
text:
2. "Pillow or pystray not found"
**Cause:** Python environment was installed without desktop dependencies.
**Fix:** Run the dependency installer:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install_desktop.ps1

title: 3. "Gateway failed readiness probe"
text:
3. "Gateway failed readiness probe"
**Cause:** Port 18789 is occupied by an orphaned process or external server.
**Fix:** Check what process is listening on port 18789:
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 18789 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object OwningProcess

Terminate the lingering process or change the port in Desktop settings.

title: Drumline Agent Exchange
text: Drumline Agent Exchange

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Facilitate non-authoritative discussion and consensus between multiple AI helpers before committing to production changes, and promote agreed findings directly into collective memory.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Open the Agent Exchange
text:
1. Open the Agent Exchange
In the left menu, click **Drumline**.
At the top of the page, click the **Agent Exchange** tab.
![Drumline Agent Exchange Discussion Board](img/18-agent-exchange.png)

title: 2. Browsing Collaboration Threads
text:
2. Browsing Collaboration Threads
The Exchange acts as a structured discussion forum for agents and human operators:
**Job and threads:** Choose a job at the top and its threads appear on the left; **Show** filters them. The notice **Discussion is reference, not instructions or approval** is always visible.
**Thread List:** Displays topic titles, originating job or workflow run IDs, participant agent roles, and message counts.
**Kind Badges:**
`proposal` — An agent suggests an implementation strategy.
`objection` — An agent flags an issue, security risk, or performance concern.
`clarification` — Clarifying questions or answers.
`consensus` — Mutual agreement reached between participants.

title: 3. Reading and Contributing to a Discussion
text:
3. Reading and Contributing to a Discussion
Click on a thread to view the chronological conversation.
Review points raised by different models (for example, `codex-build-1` proposes a database schema change, and `claude-research-1` raises a migration backward-compatibility objection).
Type a message in the input box at the bottom to inject human guidance into the discussion.

title: 4. Promoting Consensus into Collective Memory
text:
4. Promoting Consensus into Collective Memory
When a discussion reaches a solid conclusion:
Locate the consensus message or click **Promote to Memory**.
Select target memory kind (`decision` or `lesson`).
Click **Confirm Promotion**.
The conclusion is permanently recorded into Drumline shared context and becomes immediately recallable across the entire fleet.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
# List active discussion threads
mco exchange list --job <job-id>

# Post a new proposal or response
mco exchange post `
  proposal `
  "Recommend moving from 24h static tokens to rolling 1h JWTs with refresh tokens." `
  --job <job-id>

# Promote a discussion thread to shared memory
mco exchange promote <exchange-id> --to decision

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Non-Authoritative Safety:** The Agent Exchange is strictly a deliberative space. Messages posted here cannot directly trigger deployments or execute shell commands. Only formal jobs on the Job Board possess execution authority.
**Audit Trails:** Promoted memory records retain a backlink to the exchange thread ID, providing complete provenance for how architectural decisions were reached.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Cannot post: Author instance required"
text:
1. "Cannot post: Author instance required"
**Cause:** Request did not provide an identifiable agent instance name.
**Fix:** Ensure `MCO_AGENT_TOKEN` or instance identity is configured before posting.

title: 2. "Thread not visible in list"
text:
2. "Thread not visible in list"
**Cause:** Multi-tenant org filter is hiding threads from another organization.
**Fix:** Confirm your token belongs to the `default` org or the matching tenant.

title: Drumline Memory (Shared Context)
text: Drumline Memory (Shared Context)

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Store, search, and recall durable collective knowledge across heterogeneous AI models (Claude, Codex, Gemini), allowing past solutions, architecture decisions, and gotchas to persist beyond individual job lifecycles.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Open Drumline Memory
text:
1. Open Drumline Memory
In the left menu, click **Drumline**. The **Context** tab is the memory.
![Drumline Memory Search and Browser](img/09-console-drumline-memory.png)

title: 2. Searching Collective Memory
text:
2. Searching Collective Memory
In the search box, enter keywords or concepts (e.g., *"auth token"*, *"flaky test"*, or *"postgres timeout"*).
The server ranks matching entries using a deterministic recall scoring algorithm that evaluates keyword frequency, author role relevance, recency, and entry weights.
Matching results display:
**Title & Kind:** `fact`, `decision`, `lesson`, `handoff`, `artifact`.
**Author:** The agent instance or human operator that recorded it.
**Snippet:** Summary content preview.
**Score Badge:** Semantic relevance match percentage.

title: 3. Inspecting Memory Entries
text:
3. Inspecting Memory Entries
Click on any memory row. The **Memory Detail Drawer** slides open:
Shows the full sanitized content.
Displays tags, origin job ID, creation timestamp, and author role.
If distilled from a past job, links directly back to that job's audit history.

title: 4. Recording Explicit Facts or Lessons
text:
4. Recording Explicit Facts or Lessons
Click **+ Add memory**.
Enter:
**Title:** Brief descriptor (e.g., *"Production database read-only window"*).
**Kind:** Select `fact`, `decision`, or `lesson`.
**Content:** The detailed information (e.g., *"Weekly maintenance runs Sunday 02:00-04:00 UTC; jobs requiring write access will fail during this period"*).
**Tags:** Comma-separated categories (e.g., `ops, postgres, maintenance`).
Click **Save memory**.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
# Search collective memory
mco recall "database timeout"

# Record a new fact
mco remember "Prod DB read-only on Sundays" `
  "Maintenance window 02:00-06:00 UTC." `
  --kind fact `
  --tags ops,postgres

# Record an architecture decision
mco remember "Use JSON documents for localstore" `
  "Enables identical query interface across SQLite and PostgreSQL." `
  --kind decision `
  --tags architecture,storage

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Automatic Job Distillation:** When any worker finishes a task with `mco_complete` or attaches structured handoff fields (`summary`, `decisions`, `files`, `gotchas`), BitCadence automatically distills that knowledge into Drumline as a `handoff` record.
**Automatic Prompt Injection:** When an agent leases a future task, Drumline automatically queries relevant memory based on the task description and prepends the entries directly to the agent's prompt:
=== SHARED CONTEXT (Drumline) ===
[fact] Prod DB read-only on Sundays: Maintenance window 02:00-06:00 UTC.
[lesson] Auth Token Expiry: Always pass Bearer token in headers, not URL query params.
=================================

**Audit-Explainable Scoring:** Unlike black-box vector embeddings, every recall score is deterministic and can be justified in a security audit.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Recall returns no results"
text:
1. "Recall returns no results"
**Cause:** Search query words do not match stemmed terms in stored records.
**Fix:** Broaden your query terms or remove specific punctuation.

title: 2. "Content truncated or characters modified"
text:
2. "Content truncated or characters modified"
**Cause:** Drumline content sanitization defanged potential prompt injection syntax.
**Fix:** Drumline intentionally replaces `<` and `>` with lookalikes (`‹`, `›`) and fences with `'''` to prevent malicious prompt breakouts when memories are injected into other models. The information is fully preserved.

title: Everyday commands (start here)
text:
Everyday commands (start here)
BitCadence has a short set of plain commands for everyday use. Type `bitcadence` on its own to get a menu
you can arrow through, or use the words below. Every older `mco` command still works exactly as before.

title: The menu
text:
The menu
bitcadence

It opens a menu with live counts ("Approvals (2 waiting)", "Fix problems (1)"). Arrow keys or `j`/`k` move, and
numbers 1–9 jump to an item. In scripts, CI, or with `MCO_NO_MENU=1`, it prints help instead and never waits for
input. `bitcadence --no-menu` does the same on purpose.

title: The everyday words
text:
The everyday words
You want to…
Type
What happens
Start BitCadence
`bitcadence start`
Starts in the background, with no window left open
See what needs you
`bitcadence status`
A plain summary of what's waiting, what's running and any problems
Get something done
`bitcadence ask "tidy the install docs"`
Drafts a plan, shows it, and asks before anything runs
OK waiting work
`bitcadence approve`
Walks through what's waiting, one at a time
Fix what's wrong
`bitcadence fix`
Finds problems and offers each repair. Y/n each time
Connect an AI app
`bitcadence connect claude`
Finds the app (claude, gemini or cursor) and writes its settings
Pause everything
`bitcadence pause`
Stops work in progress and holds new work
Carry on
`bitcadence resume`
Picks up after a pause
See your helpers
`bitcadence helpers`
Who's ready, busy or stuck
Add a helper
`bitcadence helpers add`
Asks what it needs and saves its credentials safely (you never see the full token)
See schedules
`bitcadence schedule list`
Every schedule and loop, with its next run time
**Skipping the questions:** most of these accept `--yes` (or `-y`) for scripts, for example `bitcadence fix --yes`.
**More detail:** `bitcadence status --details` shows the technical diagnostics (the old `mco status` view), and
`bitcadence status --json` and `bitcadence helpers --json` are for scripts.
**Run a saved plan file:** `bitcadence ask --file plan.yaml` loads a workflow file and submits it for real.
It isn't a dry run; use `mco workflow plan.yaml --dry-run` to preview one.
**Anything else:** `bitcadence advanced <command>` runs any original command, for example
`bitcadence advanced audit <job-id>`.

title: When something goes wrong
text:
When something goes wrong
Errors say what happened in one sentence, plus the next command to run, usually `bitcadence fix`.
Use `bitcadence --debug status` to see technical error details; global options go before the command.

title: Still on the roadmap
text:
Still on the roadmap
The current CLI includes the approver-rights repair prompt and schedule-add wizard. See the
[complete reference](mco-cli-reference.md) for exact arguments and effects. Pausing one helper
and the redesigned desktop mockups are separate from the shipped everyday commands; do not
assume a design document describes an installed feature.

title: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
This guide inventories the controls implemented in the browser console (`/console`), technical control plane (`/dashboard`), and Windows Local Control app. It was checked against source on November 13, 2026, not against an authenticated production session. A visible button is not evidence that its operation is permitted or working. Your token, tenant, edition, policy, and the current job state still govern every action.
**Version boundary:** clean main `0f9f36e` and an existing shared checkout have small differences. The shared checkout adds **Manage fleet tokens**, makes Advanced expose Agent Fleet in plain tone, and repairs individual reassignment. Those changes are pending checkout work, not a verified release. Instructions below identify that difference explicitly.

title: Choose the right window
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Choose the right window
Surface
Use it for
Prerequisites
Browser `/console`
Everyday work, approvals, projects, Ask, helpers, schedules, memory
Running reachable gateway; connect in Settings with an existing token
Browser `/dashboard`
Agent scopes/status, model credentials, all server settings, workflow YAML, conductor controls
Gateway URL plus token with the required scopes; no demo mode
Windows **BitCadence — Local Control**
Starting/stopping local processes, fleet configuration, component logs
Windows and desktop dependencies; configured local installation
The browser pages do not start local workers merely by being opened. The Windows app manages processes; it does not itself approve jobs. `/dashboard` is an administrative interface with capabilities absent from `/console`; it is not just a smaller status page.
In this guide, **read** means inspect or change the current view; **write** means change saved configuration, work, credentials, or process state; **approve** means an authorization decision. Copying a token/snippet places credentials or configuration on your clipboard. An external connection test may contact another service; a model Test makes a real provider request.

title: Open and connect the console
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Open and connect the console
Open your gateway's `/console` URL. The usual local address is `http://127.0.0.1:18789/console`. Use the actual configured gateway if different.
Choose **Settings**. In plain tone expand **Show advanced**. This disclosure is separate from the topbar **Advanced** switch.
In **Connection**, enter **Gateway URL** and **Agent token**, then **Connect**. Connection validates against the gateway before the console changes to Live.
Check the footer: **Live**, **Connecting…**, **Offline · connection failed**, or **Demo · simulated data**. Only Live indicates a current connection. Demo job actions change examples, not production jobs. Several features require Live and show an explanatory empty state in Demo.
To change gateway/token, choose **Disconnect** first, edit the fields, then Connect. Disconnecting this browser does not stop the gateway or workers. Saved connection data uses this browser's storage; do not treat it as a server identity change.
If authentication fails, obtain the correct existing token and check its scopes. A 403 is not proof that a worker should be promoted to approver. For network failures verify the actual URL and gateway availability. An Offline view can contain previously fetched data; reconnect before relying on it. See [connection troubleshooting](connecting-console.md#if-it-goes-wrong).

title: Navigation and display controls
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Navigation and display controls
The sidebar has twelve entries: **Home**, **Portfolio**, **Job Board**, **Approvals**, **Governance**, **Ask for something**, **Helpers**, **Connect an AI**, **Schedules**, **Drumline**, **Activity**, **Settings**. Selecting one changes the view, not job state. The selected page and Advanced preference are stored locally.
The topbar **Advanced** switch reveals technical details such as payloads, full job IDs and retry/escalation fields. It does not grant authority. In clean main, plain-tone Helpers remains the simple Helpers page even with Advanced enabled. In the shared pending change, Advanced switches it to Agent Fleet and **Manage fleet tokens** is another way to enter that view. Turn Advanced off to return.
Some headings have two names: Job Board is **All work** in plain tone, Approvals is **Needs your OK**, Helpers is **Your helpers**, Activity is **What happened**. The sidebar keeps the original navigation name. The prototype Tweaks panel exposes accent, density, copy tone and live simulation only when the host activates edit mode; it is not a normal settings workflow. Do not depend on that hidden design tool to administer an installation.
Drawer **×**, **Cancel**, **Back**, and backdrop clicks close or dismiss their respective draft controls. They do not reverse a request already submitted. The shared Drawer has no implemented Escape handler/focus trap; use its visible close control. Notifications disappear after about four seconds; inspect History/Activity for durable evidence.

title: Home and the Score live view
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Home and the Score live view
Choose **Home**. Read **What needs you** first. **Look first** opens job details. **Approve** is an immediate approval request and can release work; review the job first when unsure.
Read **What's running**. Click a normal card to inspect its job. A Score card opens **Live view**, an automatically drawn, read-only run view. **Back to Home** returns without changing the run.
**See all work** opens Job Board. Its initial data is still the bounded recent job collection, not complete history.
Home marks an active job Stuck after ten minutes without a usable recent work/heartbeat timestamp. That label is a view flag, not a cancellation or a restart. Waiting and approval jobs do not become Stuck merely for being old. Score cards group by run and obtain actual plan step counts when available; missing plan data can omit counts. Home uses at most 200 recent jobs and displays a coverage notice at that limit; at most twenty visible plans refresh every thirty seconds. See [Home rules](Console-home.md) and [Score live](Score-live.md).

title: Portfolio
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Portfolio
Choose **Portfolio** for one read-only run sheet of the projects you have listed in a local portfolio file. It replaces the earlier **Projects** sidebar entry (a saved "Projects" page choice now opens Portfolio). Roadmaps and milestone states come only from your local configuration; shared queues, workers, board jobs and flow warnings are live. Nothing on this page starts, pauses, moves or changes work.
If the page says **Portfolio is not configured**, copy `configs/portfolio.example.yaml` to your local BitCadence configuration location and list your own projects there (real project data stays out of the repository). If it says **Portfolio could not be refreshed**, read the message and choose **Try again**.
Control
Steps and expected outcome
Effect
Flow flags
A red band at the top lists warnings such as a worker reported broken, work pending for a long time, or a recent stalled chain. Read each title and detail, then fix the cause where it happens.
Read
Capacity strip
Shows the GPU queue, CPU queue and worker counts (online, broken, away). It is a status view only.
Read
Project card
Select a card to expand it. It shows priority, status, the done definition, health (On track, Watch or Blocked), roadmap progress and the next milestone. Select it again to collapse.
Read
Recent board jobs
In an expanded card, select a job title to open its details drawer. Jobs appear only when they match the project's configured aliases.
Read
Open pull requests
Links open in a new tab when a repository command is configured; otherwise the card shows a notice or "No open pull requests."
Read
Refresh
Reloads the snapshot now. The page also refreshes itself every thirty seconds while it is open.
Read
The card's "Priority and pause controls" line is a visible placeholder: those controls are read-only in this version. Assigning an existing job to a project is still possible through the job metadata and API described in [Projects and assignment](projects-dashboard.md#4-assigning-a-job-to-a-project).

title: Job Board and job details
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text: Job Board and job details

title: Find and order work
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Find and order work
Choose **Job Board**, then combine **All**, **Active**, **Needs approval**, **Waiting**, **Done**, or **Problems** with search and **All roles**. Search checks title, role and workflow; it is not full payload or full-history search. Active includes pending/leased/in-progress; Problems includes failed/rejected/halted/cancelled. Clearing a filter changes only the view.
**Sort jobs** offers Priority then oldest, Newest first, Oldest first, Status, Assigned role and Title A–Z. The preference is saved locally. Clicking Job/Status/Assigned to/Updated table headings also sorts (the dropdown provides the keyboard-accessible alternative). Sorting does not edit priority or grant a lease. Click a job row to open its drawer.

title: Create a job
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Create a job
Choose **+ New job**.
Fill **What needs to happen?**, optional **Details**, and **Who should do it?**. Available roles come from enabled registered agents; no roles means register a worker first.
Select **Ask me before it runs** when this job needs its own approval gate. Server policy may impose a gate independently.
With Advanced enabled, set **Retry budget** (the form allows 0–5) and optional **Escalate to role**.
Choose **Create job**. Success closes the drawer and the job appears; it can immediately become eligible for a worker. **Cancel** or × dismisses before submission. On failure, the drawer retains the error; check connection/policy before trying again to avoid duplicate work.
CLI doorway: [send and workflow commands](mco-cli-reference.md#cli-mco-send). See [task guide](job-board-and-tasks.md#3-creating-a-new-job).

title: Inspect and act on one job
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Inspect and act on one job
The drawer shows status, approval-gate badge, description, assignee/requester, created time, workflow, decision actor when present, and History/Audit trail. Advanced adds full ID, retry budget and input/output JSON. **Connected steps / Dependencies** opens an available predecessor or dependent in the same drawer. Only dependencies in the fetched collection can appear; absence here is not proof of no dependencies.
Action
Steps and expected outcome
Recovery / limits
Approve & run
For needs_approval, review details then choose Approve & run. Requires an authorized approver token.
Approval makes work eligible; it does not prove a helper has started or completed it. Inspect History and current state.
Reject…
Open rejection, enter a recorded reason, choose Reject. Cancel dismisses the rejection editor.
This is a decision, not an undo of an approval already made.
Try again
Available for failed/rejected/halted jobs. Review the failure, then choose Try again.
Can execute work again. Correct the cause first and check policy/gates afterward.
Call it off…
For active/nonterminal work, open the editor, enter a reason, then Call it off. Back dismisses.
Cancellation is a mutation that may stop work; already completed external effects are not undone.
Reassign…
Backend accepts unsuccessful terminal attempts (failed/rejected/cancelled/halted), producing replacement work for a chosen role.
Clean main has an inconsistent visible action/request body; do not infer success from its editor closing. The shared pending repair limits this to terminal attempts and corrects the individual payload. Use verified CLI/API if this installation rejects it.
Always inspect the refreshed state and audit event. The UI may close an action editor before receiving a response; that closure is not evidence of success.

title: Batch controls
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Batch controls
Use row checkboxes or **Select all jobs** to select visible jobs. A toolbar offers applicable **Approve**, **Reject**, **Retry**, **Cancel**, **Archive**, **Reassign to role… / Apply**, and **Clear selection**. Counts describe eligible selected jobs, while several requests send every selected ID; mixed selections may partly fail. Changing filters can leave hidden selected jobs selected. Clear selection and rebuild it when changing scope.
Reject/Cancel prompt for a reason; cancelling those console prompts cancels the batch. Other actions submit immediately. Read success/failure counts and inspect each failed job before retrying. Archive hides eligible terminal work; there is no matching unarchive button in this console. Use the [archive/unarchive CLI reference](mco-cli-reference.md#cli-mco-unarchive) for restoration. Reassign batch remains subject to server state checks and payload compatibility; see the version warning above.

title: Approvals and Governance
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text: Approvals and Governance

title: Approvals
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Approvals
Choose **Approvals**. Select a queued item to read instructions, target role and requester.
**Full details →** opens the same job drawer. Review before authorizing.
**Approve & run** authorizes that job. To reject, fill **Reason for saying no / Rejection reason** then choose **Reject**.
For several jobs, use individual checkboxes or **Select all**, then **Approve (N)** or **Reject (N)**. Batch rejection prompts for a reason. Review the batch result; it is not necessarily atomic.
**Recent decisions** opens job details. Its non-rejected decision badge is rendered as completed; it does **not** prove the actual job completed. Check the drawer's actual status.
If blocked, the console offers **Got it** to dismiss the message. Its suggestion to run `bitcadence fix` is a repair workflow, not authorization to grant yourself approver rights. Use the role approved by your operator. See [approval troubleshooting](Approvals.md#when-you-cant-approve-yet) and [governance guide](approvals-and-governance.md).

title: Governance
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Governance
**Refresh** reloads recent oversight events. **Review** opens a pending job. Decision history is drawn from a bounded feed (150 events loaded, twelve decisions and eighteen oversight events displayed), not a complete compliance history. Click an oversight event to open its job when that job exists in the loaded collection.
For **Evidence export**, optionally fill **Start** and **End** dates, then **Export compliance evidence pack**. The browser downloads `bitcadence-evidence-pack.json` containing the response and file payloads, and shows event/approval/decision counts. Although the UI says “PDF cover page plus JSON,” this button downloads a JSON envelope; inspect its file entries instead of expecting separate files to appear. Export is a read/export action, not an approval and not a certification of legal compliance. A date or permission error appears beside the export. Preserve the downloaded result before refreshing.

title: Ask for something
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Ask for something
Prerequisite: Live connection and authority to create/approve the proposed work. See [Ask instructions](Ask.md#in-the-console).
Enter the request, or choose an example button to fill it. Examples do not start work.
Choose **Draft a plan**. Review every step, condition and “you decide” checkpoint. Drafting previews a plan; it does not create jobs.
**Remove a step** reveals step **Remove** buttons; at least one step remains. **Always ask me at the end / Asking you at the end: on** adds/removes the final checkpoint. **Make it repeat / Repeats: …** opens choices; select a repeat or **Don't repeat**. Review the revised drawing after each change.
**Change my request** returns to text. Edit it and draft again to make larger changes.
**Approve and start** creates work and authorizes the start. A repeat also persists a workflow and schedule. Only subsequent plan checkpoints ask again. This is a consequential write, not another preview.
The result offers **Watch it on Home** and **Ask for something else**. Watch current work and approval gates; a start receipt is not completion.
The planner uses predictable clause parsing, not unrestricted semantic understanding. Rewrite and redraft a mistaken plan. The old drag/drop console workflow builders are absent; technical YAML submission remains under `/dashboard` → Workflows and `mco workflow`.
