title: Everyday Helpers
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Everyday Helpers
Choose **Helpers** in plain tone. Each card combines a shape, word and light with what the helper is doing and last contact. The list refreshes every fifteen seconds. Ready/Working presence is useful evidence but does not prove a worker can complete a particular task.
**+ Add a helper** opens AI and Name fields. Choose an offered AI, enter a name, then **Add helper**. Registration/sign-in is saved on the gateway computer; it is not a completed work test. Cancel closes the form. See [add a helper](Helpers.md#add-a-helper).
**Fix it** first requests a diagnosis. Review every proposed change in **Here's what I found**. **Not now** dismisses it without applying. **Yes, fix it** applies the proposed repair and returns results. This is a repair of the helper set, not necessarily only the card you clicked; inspect the full plan. Review permissions and active work before confirming. See [repair workflow](Helpers.md#fix-it).

title: Agent Fleet / tokens
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Agent Fleet / tokens
Use `/dashboard` → Agents & Tokens for a reliable administrative doorway on clean main. The shared pending console change exposes **Manage fleet tokens** and Advanced Agent Fleet. In that view:
**Add agent / Register agent** opens Instance ID, Role, and (with Advanced) Org. Enter the intended identity and an already configured tenant, then **Add agent / Register**.
Copy the resulting once-shown token using **Copy**, securely configure the intended worker, then **Done / Close**. Registration itself does not start a listener.
**New token / Reset token** asks for confirmation. It immediately invalidates the old token. Copy and install the replacement; there is no undo that restores the old secret.
**Remove** confirms immediate token invalidation and deletes the registration if server policy allows it. It is not the correct way to stop an actively leased worker. Inspect current leases and obey server refusal.
**Move…** appears for a host operator with multiple tenants. Choose a target, **Confirm**, then accept the boundary warning. Cancel dismisses. Agent visibility/management changes with its tenant; do not mistake an agent disappearing from this view for deletion.
Per-role online counts, current job and Advanced completed counts reflect the fetched collection. See [fleet guide](agent-fleet-and-presence.md) for CLI equivalents and lost-token recovery. Copy feedback or a displayed token is not evidence the executor now uses it.

title: Connect an AI
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Connect an AI
This page edits client app configuration on the **gateway computer**. A remote browser does not make its own laptop's app configuration available to the gateway.
Choose **Connect an AI** after connecting the console itself. These are different connections.
For an installed app card choose **Connect**. Read the result and restart the target app if instructed. Existing configuration is backed up; unrelated settings are preserved by the connector's implementation.
**Send a test** checks the configured entry and executable availability. It is not proof that the target app completed a live MCP call/job.
**Disconnect** removes BitCadence's entry; it does not shut down the gateway. Verify the target app after restarting it.
For **Another app**, choose **Show me a code**, then **Copy**. Paste the snippet into the intended supported client's connection configuration. Treat any embedded credential as a secret. The button returns configuration rather than installing an arbitrary client.
Not found: install the app on the gateway host, then revisit/reload the page. For malformed configuration the connector should return an error rather than silently replace it; inspect the backup before recovery. See [supported apps and tests](Connect-an-AI.md#apps).

title: Schedules
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Schedules
Reading needs `jobs:read`; adding/toggling needs `agents:manage`. A running scheduler is required for saved schedules to execute.
Choose **Schedules**. Existing cards show name, schedule sentence, next run and **On / Off**.
To create one, select **What should run?** from configured launchers. If none appear, create eligible work first; this page does not offer arbitrary app/page launches.
Choose **Every day**, **Every weekday**, **Certain days**, or **Every hour** as offered by the server. For Certain days toggle each day; at least one is required. For non-hourly frequencies set **At what time?**.
Read the sentence preview. Choose **Save** to persist; verify its card and next-run text.
Click an existing card's **On/Off** to change whether it runs. This saves immediately and can be reversed with the same control. It does not delete the schedule or cancel work already launched.
**Time-zone limitation:** the UI claims it detects “your computer” but does not send a browser zone. The backend detects the gateway host's zone. On remote gateways, verify the actual server zone/next-run time before enabling; see [scheduling configuration](scheduling-and-loops.md#2-configure-launchers-and-loops). There is no GUI timezone selector, delete button or full schedule editor here. [Plain schedule commands](Schedules.md#add-one) and the advanced scheduler configuration handle the remaining operations.

title: Drumline: Context and Agent Exchange
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Drumline: Context and Agent Exchange
Use **Drumline**, then **Context** or **Agent Exchange**. Arrow keys switch these two tabs. The last subview is stored locally. Both use the live gateway; tenant isolation still applies.

title: Context
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Context
Enter **Search memory / Recall query** and optional comma-separated tags, then **Search / Recall**. Tags constrain results; the server ranks recall. At most 25 entries are requested.
**Show more / Collapse** expands entry text; **Drill down →** opens provenance/full text. The detail drawer includes provenance and **Copy text**; **Open Source Job** opens the linked job when available in the loaded collection. Advanced adds weight metadata.
**+ Add memory / + Remember** opens Title, Kind, Tags and Content. Fill title and content, choose the kind, then **Save memory / Remember**. This creates shared context that eligible agents can recall. The composer **Cancel** dismisses before saving; no edit/delete/undo button is exposed here.
Empty search: clear tags and reword the query before assuming the knowledge is absent. Distillation and injection settings affect whether memory is created/recalled; a saved memory is not a guarantee it appears in every future prompt. See [memory instructions](drumline-memory.md#step-by-step-instructions).

title: Agent Exchange
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Agent Exchange
Discussion is reference, not instructions or approval. Posting a “decision” does not authorize a job. Discussion enters recalled Context only through explicit promotion.
Choose **Job**, optionally filter **Show / kind**, then select a thread. Read author, replies and Resolved/Replaced/Promoted badges.
To start a thread, choose Type (question, proposal, blocker, decision, handoff), enter **Message** (8,000-character UI maximum), and **Post**.
**Reply**, **Resolve**, and **Replace** prepare a typed response to a message. Enter the explanation and Post; opening the composer alone changes nothing. **Cancel reply/resolution/supersession** returns to a new root message.
A decision or handoff offers **Promote to context**. Review the warning and preview, select Decision/Lesson/Handoff, optionally give a title, then **Promote to …**. This copies sanitized text into shared Context with a receipt. **Cancel** dismisses the promotion form. Resolution/replacement/promotion are recorded actions, not deletion of the original discussion.
If author identity is missing or a job is not in the picker, verify connection, tenant and loaded job window. Do not recreate discussion blindly. See [exchange guide](drumline-agent-exchange.md#step-by-step-instructions).

title: Activity
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Activity
Choose **Activity** for a cross-job audit view. In Live mode, enter search text (event/job/actor), choose event type, then **Refresh** to reload the current window. **Load more** increases the requested event limit; it does not broaden the ordinary job collection. Click a row only when its linked job is loaded. Advanced adds detail JSON, abbreviated in this table; use job History for fuller context.
The statistics summarize fetched events/jobs: Events in last day, failure rate, typical approval wait, and distinct active actors. They are not independently queried system-wide metrics. Refresh/load more before drawing conclusions about missing events; search filters only the fetched window. Demo shows a connection-required explanation. See [Home guide's Activity doorway](overview-dashboard.md#4-look-at-the-rest-of-the-menu).

title: Everyday settings
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Everyday settings
Plain Settings shows **Pause everything / Pause / Resume**, phone notification status, and a Memory pointer. The phone card is status-only; configuration is under Show advanced, and the text also points to `bitcadence settings`.
**Critical wording correction:** Pause writes `MCO_KILL_SWITCH`; despite the plain card saying “Jobs in progress finish,” the backend halts active attempts and pauses intake/leasing. Resume clears the pause; halted jobs require an explicit retry and do not automatically continue. Inspect current jobs, choose Pause only when that is intended, and verify History. This differs from `/dashboard`'s **Pause Conductor**, which controls the conductor sweep. Neither is a browser Disconnect.

title: Show advanced
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Show advanced
Expand **Show advanced** to reveal Connection, Experience, Gateway controls, Connectors and optional Tenancy. Connection was covered above. Experience's **Advanced mode** is the same local preference as the topbar switch, not a permission grant.
**Gateway controls** displays governance, notifications, presence and memory fields from server metadata. Edit the intended fields, then **Save gateway settings**; this console sends changed fields and reloads their values. A success message means settings saved and audited, not that queued jobs finished. Raw choice settings currently render as text fields in this component; use exactly the allowed values or use `/dashboard`, which renders choices as dropdowns.
**Connectors:** enter ServiceNow or Dynatrace fields, then **Save connectors** before **Test connection**. Secret fields start blank; blank keeps the existing secret. Test uses saved gateway configuration, not unsaved form text. A successful Test reveals **Sync now**, which can import/create/update work; it is a write, not another health probe. Inspect the resulting created/updated/skipped summary. A locked encrypted secret store must be unlocked through the supported setup workflow; do not put secrets into plaintext as a workaround.
**Tenancy** (Advanced and host-operator authority) lists configured orgs and in-use markers. Enter a new org name (1–64 letters/digits or `. _ : -`) and **Add org**. This persists the allowed-org list; it does not move existing jobs or agents. There is no remove/rename org button here. Use Fleet's Move or the technical admin surface only within authorized tenant boundaries.
For the full server-driven settings catalogue and groups omitted by this console, use [technical control-plane settings](#technical-control-plane-settings). See also [settings guide](settings-and-configuration.md).

title: Unlock and Lock
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Unlock and Lock
Open the gateway's `/dashboard`, paste an existing bearer token and choose **Unlock** (Enter also works). Authentication probes job access, then opens Operations. Scoped tokens can still receive permission errors on other pages; Unlock does not make them admins. **Lock** clears this page's stored token and hides its shell; it does not revoke the token, stop workers, or clear the separate console's saved connection. There is no Demo mode.

title: Operations and conductor
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Operations and conductor
Operations refreshes approximately every five seconds. Click Job/Title/Status/Priority/Target/Leased By/Created headings to toggle sorting. Use **Audit** to show a job's event text. **Approve / Reject** act on a queued gate; rejection prompts for a reason. **Retry** appears beside failed/rejected work.
Row and header checkboxes fill a shared selection across Approval Queue and Job Board. **Approve**, **Reject**, **Retry**, **Cancel**, **Archive**, **Reassign**, and **Clear** appear in the bulk bar. Reassign prompts for a role. Read result counts; partial errors are possible. **Known limitation:** cancelling the dashboard's Cancel-reason prompt still proceeds with an empty reason; do not use that prompt's Cancel as an abort mechanism. Use Clear before selecting a batch action. Individual Reject similarly turns prompt cancellation into an empty rejection request.
**Autonomy Engine** shows conductor state, sweep interval, shadow/live-write status and active-run count. **Pause / Resume** changes conductor sweeps; **Tick Now** triggers a real manual sweep that may advance jobs. These are writes and do not grant new authority or change shadow/live policy.
**Live Look** reads autonomy state and opens a modal with active/failing runs, database location and repository-write status. Its **Trigger Sweep Now**, **Pause Conductor / Resume Conductor** and each **Abort Run** mutate live state. **Close** or the backdrop dismisses the modal. **Known limitation:** Abort Run's reason prompt treats Cancel as “Aborted by operator” and still submits the abort. Do not click Abort Run merely to inspect it. This technical Live Look is different from Home's read-only Score drawing.
CLI doorway: [Scores and autonomy](scores-and-autonomy.md). A ready server, active conductor or visible run is not end-to-end evidence of work delivery.

title: Agents & Tokens
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Agents & Tokens
Choose **Agents & Tokens**, then **+ Register agent**.
Fill Name, Role and offered Org. Select explicit Scopes only when needed; none checked requests role-derived defaults. **Register & generate token** submits; **Cancel** dismisses.
The token modal has **Copy token**, **Done**, plus worker/MCP configuration **Copy** controls. Save the once-shown token and configure the intended executor. Copy is not a listener start/test.
Existing **Edit** changes Role, Status (online/offline/disabled) and Scopes; **Save** submits, Cancel dismisses. This is access administration, not a harmless display preference. A manually set online status is not proof of heartbeat/execution.
**Reset token** asks confirmation, invalidates the old token and shows the replacement once. **Delete** confirms registration/token removal. Respect active-lease refusals. See [fleet troubleshooting](agent-fleet-and-presence.md#if-it-goes-wrong).

title: Model Connections
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Model Connections
These stored provider connections are for custom workers/executors. Adding one does not select or change a model for every agent.
Choose **Model Connections → + Add connection**.
Enter Name, choose an offered Provider, fill Base URL when the provider allows it, optional Model, and API key. **Add & save** persists; Cancel dismisses.
**Test** makes a real provider call and returns success/failure, detail and latency. It can consume provider quota; run it intentionally.
**Edit** can change Name, editable Base URL, Model and New API key. Blank key preserves the existing secret. **Save** submits; Cancel dismisses.
**Delete** confirms removal of the connection and stored key. It has no undelete control. Preserve needed configuration through your authorized secret/configuration process before deletion.
Recover from validation/auth/network errors by checking saved provider/endpoint/model/key, then retest once corrected. A successful credential test does not prove a fleet worker uses that connection.

title: Workflows
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Workflows
Choose **Workflows**, paste valid workflow YAML, review roles, dependencies, conditions and approval flags, then **Submit workflow**. This creates governed jobs and shows run/job JSON; it is not a preview or dry-run. Use the CLI/offline validation path in [workflow guide](workflows-and-flow-control.md#the-cli-equivalent) before submission when needed. On parse/cycle/policy failure, correct the input; on ambiguous network failure inspect existing runs/jobs before resubmitting.

title: Windows Local Control and tray
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Windows Local Control and tray
See [installation/shortcut setup](desktop-app-and-tray.md#1-installation-one-click-installer-desktop-shortcut). The following controls are verified in `src/mco/desktop/app.py` and `controller.py`; no live start/stop was performed for this guide.
Control
Steps and actual scope
Expected feedback / recovery
Start all
Starts gateway, waits for readiness, then scheduler and configured enabled workers. Already-running external matches are recognized.
Inspect each row, not only global Gateway ready. Worker failures can be reported while other components start.
Stop all
Stops configured components, including exact matching external processes belonging to the same user, and disables/ends their scheduled tasks.
Can interrupt active executors. Inspect component rows and logs; it is broader than Exit.
Restart all
Stop all then Start all.
May interrupt active work and leave scheduled tasks disabled. Verify the complete stack afterward.
Component row
Select a row to filter the bottom log viewer to its last 100 lines. State/Process/Last error show component evidence.
External workers retain their original logs; an empty app log is not evidence they are silent.
Start selected
Select the intended component then Start selected.
Gateway must be ready before scheduler/workers. No selection is a silent no-op. Only the first selected row is used.
Stop selected
Select the intended component then Stop selected.
Stops its process tree/exact external match and disables its matching scheduled task.
Restart selected
Select the component then Restart selected.
Stop then start; inspect the row and work ownership before/after.
Open console
Opens the configured local `/console` in the default browser.
It does not start the server or authenticate that browser automatically.
Fleet settings
Opens the fleet TOML in Notepad, creating a starter file if absent. Save intentionally.
This button can write/create a file even before Reload. See [fleet schema](sidecars-and-fleet-daemons.md#supported-fields).
Reload settings
Reloads fleet definitions. Removed or changed workers can be stopped as part of reconciliation.
This is not a read-only refresh. Inspect changed worker rows, then explicitly start what should run.
Move workers into app
Disables matching recurring tasks, Stop all, then Start all under app supervision.
This is a consequential handoff that interrupts process trees. Do between jobs with appropriate authorization, not as a cosmetic warning dismissal.
Window X
Hides the window if tray support exists; otherwise exits.
Tray fallback explicitly warns that close exits.
Right-click the tray icon: **Open BitCadence** restores the control window; **Start all**, **Stop all** and **Open console** have the same scope as above; **Exit** shuts down only supervisor-owned child processes and exits. Exact external workers remain unless Stop was used. A second shortcut launch brings forward the existing app; `--start-all` can also request a start in that instance.
“Scheduled workers are still enabled” means duplicate-start protection refused a new app-owned worker. Existing scheduled workers may still run. Either keep their current management or intentionally use Move workers into app between jobs. Do not kill arbitrary Python processes or erase `~/.mco` as a first recovery step. Read the specific component Last error and original log. Readiness alone does not establish a usable fleet.
Autostart is configured through the [autostart script](desktop-app-and-tray.md#5-configuring-autostart-on-sign-in), not a checkbox in this window. There is no GUI port editor or updater; launcher options/configuration and the documented installation update process provide those capabilities.

title: Coverage and limits
page: GUI reference: console, control plane, and Windows app
text:
Coverage and limits
The machine-readable [GUI feature coverage](_review/gui-feature-coverage.json) maps control/workflow groups to source and this guide. It includes twelve console pages, the read-only Score view and drawers, five technical control-plane pages/lock/modal flows, Windows window/tray actions and every current server-driven setting. It also marks unreachable legacy console components and pending checkout changes.
This is static source verification. Authentication, browser keyboard/assistive-technology behavior, remote host differences, external provider tests, downloads, live job transitions and Windows task handoffs require separate controlled runtime checks. No production jobs, schedules, tokens, services, approvals or GPU work were changed while writing it. Proposed improvements and known mismatches are in [UX review](UX-REVIEW.md).

title: Helpers
text:
Helpers
Open `/console` and choose **Helpers**, or run `bitcadence helpers` in a
terminal. Both show the same thing: each helper's friendly name, a health light
with a word, and what it is doing in plain words.

title: The light and the word
text:
The light and the word
Light
Word
Meaning
● green
Working
It has a job right now.
● green
Ready
It is connected and waiting for a job.
▲ red
Stuck
Something needs fixing (see Fix it).
○ grey
Not connected
No sign of life.
○ grey
Paused
Turned off on purpose.
Colour is never the only signal: every light has a shape and its word. A name
like `claude-worker_3` is shown as "Claude worker 3". Each card also says when
the helper was last heard from. Tokens and credentials are never on this page.

title: Add a helper
text:
Add a helper
**+ Add a helper** asks which AI should power it (Claude, ChatGPT / Codex,
Gemini / Antigravity) and a name. It uses the same code as
`bitcadence helpers add`: the helper is registered and its sign-in is saved on
this computer. The page confirms "Penny is added" and never shows the sign-in; the
terminal shows it only masked, as `mco_tok_...1a2b`. An existing helper's name is
refused instead of silently replacing its sign-in.
bitcadence helpers add --name penny --role codex

title: Fix it
text:
Fix it
Two problems look fine from outside, so BitCadence checks for them:
**A locked notes file.** Another BitCadence process has the helper's
`<name>.log` open, so it cannot save its notes. The light turns red even
though the helper looks online.
**Two copies running.** More than one `wake` process is watching the same
helper. The oldest copy stays; the extras are stopped.
**Fix it** looks first and changes nothing: it lists what it found and what it
would do. Only after you answer **Yes, fix it** (in a terminal, `Y`) does it stop
the extra copy. Without an answer, nothing is stopped. A program that is not
BitCadence is never stopped; you are told to close it yourself.
bitcadence helpers fix
bitcadence fix

`--yes` skips the question for scripts. In the gateway API, `POST
/api/helpers/fix` is a dry run unless the body has `"confirm": true`.
Checking for these problems reads the list of running programs on this computer
only. It does not change anything, and a program it is not allowed to inspect is
skipped.

title: Get comfortable with BitCadence
text:
Get comfortable with BitCadence
Give your AI helpers a clear job. See what is happening. Stay in control of what happens next.
Start with the short guides below. The complete references are here for a particular command, option or screen.

title: Your first useful task
text:
Your first useful task
**[Install and open BitCadence](install-first-run.md).** Start the local gateway and open the console. Prefer the [Windows desktop app](desktop-app-and-tray.md) for a window and tray icon.

title: Install & First Run
text: Install & First Run

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Install BitCadence on your machine with zero configuration, create an isolated local Python environment, initialize a secure operator access token, and start the system for the first time.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions (Windows One-Click)
text: Step-by-Step Instructions (Windows One-Click)

title: 1. Download and Extract BitCadence
text:
1. Download and Extract BitCadence
Download the BitCadence repository archive or clone it into a local folder on your computer (for example, `C:\BitCadence` or `C:\AI\baton\Batoncadence`).

title: 2. Run the Installer
text:
2. Run the Installer
Double-click **`install.bat`** located in the root folder of the BitCadence project.
Alternatively, launch PowerShell in that folder and run:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1

The script automatically executes six distinct setup stages:
**Python Check:** Locates an existing Python 3.9+ installation, or automatically prompts to install it via Windows Package Manager (`winget`).
**Virtual Environment:** Generates an isolated `.venv` directory to keep all project dependencies self-contained.
**Editable Installation:** Installs BitCadence (`mco`) and required libraries in development/editable mode.
**Configuration Generation:** Creates a global configuration at `~/.mco/.env` with the `Local-Only` profile and mints a high-entropy bearer token (`mco_tok_...`).
**Path Integration:** Adds `mco` to your user `PATH` (under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\BitCadence\bin`).
**Desktop Shortcut:** Creates a desktop shortcut named **BitCadence** that points to `Start BitCadence.bat`.
![BitCadence Installation and Startup Terminal](img/20-install-cli-start.png)

title: 3. Launching BitCadence
text:
3. Launching BitCadence
When the installer asks:
Would you like to start BitCadence now? [Y/n]

Press **Enter**.
The server window appears, displays your generated access token, copies it automatically to your Windows clipboard, and opens your default web browser to `http://127.0.0.1:18789/console`.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
For power users or headless environments, you can perform the entire installation manually:
# 1. Create virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# 2. Install BitCadence dependencies
pip install -e .

# 3. Create global configuration home
mkdir -p "$HOME\.mco"

# 4. Generate token and environment file
$TOKEN = "mco_tok_" + [System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N")
@"
MCO_PROFILE=Local-Only
OPERATOR_NAME=$env:USERNAME
MCO_LOCAL_TOKEN=$TOKEN
"@ | Out-File -Encoding ascii "$HOME\.mco\.env"

# 5. Start the gateway server
mco serve

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
A black command window titled **BitCadence Server** displaying:
============================================================
  Starting BitCadence...
============================================================

  Your access token (already copied to clipboard):

    mco_tok_a1b2c3d4e5f6...

  In 5 seconds your browser will open the console.
  Paste the token into the "Agent token" box and click Connect.

  Keep this window open while BitCadence is running.
  Close it to stop BitCadence.
============================================================

Your web browser will open to the BitCadence Web Console at `http://127.0.0.1:18789/console`.
In the background, SQLite databases and keys are stored locally in your user profile:
Configuration: `~/.mco/.env`
Embedded Document Store: `~/.mco/local.db`
Secrets Vault: `~/.mco/secrets.enc`

title: Linux & macOS State
text:
Linux & macOS State
BitCadence is engineered with platform neutrality in its Python core:
**macOS / Linux Installer:** Run `curl -sSf https://bitcadence.ai/install.sh | bash` or execute `bash scripts/install.sh` from the repository root.
**Service Deployment:** On Linux, `mco service install` provisions standard `systemd` unit files under `~/.config/systemd/user/bitcadence.service`.
**Desktop Manager Constraint:** The native desktop GUI supervisor (`src/mco/desktop/app.py` and `mco tray`) uses Windows Tkinter and Windows Job Objects. On Linux and macOS, users interact with BitCadence through the `mco` CLI and the browser-based web console (`http://localhost:18789/console`).
**Keychain / Secret Store:** On Windows, the secret store automatically leverages Windows Credential Manager. On Linux/macOS, auto-unlock uses the `MCO_VAULT_MASTER_KEY` environment variable.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Python was not found" or setup window closes immediately
text:
1. "Python was not found" or setup window closes immediately
**Cause:** Execution policy restrictions or missing Python on your system PATH.
**Fix:** Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:
winget install --id Python.Python.3.12 -e

Then restart your terminal and re-run `install.bat`.

title: 2. "Port 18789 is already in use"
text:
2. "Port 18789 is already in use"
**Cause:** Another instance of BitCadence or another local development server is bound to port 18789.
**Fix:** Specify an alternate port when running `mco serve`:
mco serve --port 18790

Then navigate in your browser to `http://127.0.0.1:18790/console`.

title: 3. "Cannot connect to server in browser"
text:
3. "Cannot connect to server in browser"
**Cause:** The server process was closed, or Windows Defender Firewall blocked loopback traffic.
**Fix:** Keep the command window open while working. Test loopback health directly in terminal:
curl http://127.0.0.1:18789/healthz

If it returns `{"status":"ok"}`, the server is running normally.

title: Jev decision-provider contract
text:
Jev decision-provider contract
BitCadence integrates TypeSafe/Jev as an optional semantic decision primitive,
not as an agent or general authority system. The provider is disabled by
default and ordinary BitCadence startup performs no TypeSafe network request.

title: Why Jev is here
text:
Why Jev is here
The same expensive generative agent should not have to deliberate over every
small routing, relevance, or triage question. Jev supplies fast, typed semantic
judgments for bounded questions; Claude, Codex, and other workers handle the
longer reasoning and execution. This is a two-speed workflow, not a second
authority system. Jev can suggest what a task *means*. Deterministic policy
still decides which models are eligible, how much work may run, whether a lease
is valid, and whether an effect needs a human grant or review. Jev does not
create grants, approve checkpoints, or authorize effects.
No speed or cost improvement is claimed without a measured BitCadence benchmark.
The shipped Codex and Claude task/model routes are advisory. Drumline,
watchdog, and notification use Jev only for annotations. A Jev outage or
abstention returns a deterministic fallback, not permission to skip a gate.

title: Configuration
text:
Configuration
The admin API is `/api/jev`:
`GET /api/jev` reports offline capability state and never returns a secret.
`PUT /api/jev` accepts `mode`, `model`, `timeout_seconds`, `max_retries`, and
an optional `api_key`. The key is stored through the tenant-scoped
`SecretVault` reference `typesafe-jev/api_key`; it is never written to the
provider metadata or returned by the API.
`POST /api/jev/test` is the only configuration operation that deliberately
performs model discovery against TypeSafe.
Modes are `disabled`, `shadow`, `assist`, and `active`. `jev-latest` is allowed
only for shadow evaluation. Assist and active modes require an exact model
name, and a response from any other model becomes a deterministic fallback.

title: First-time setup on Windows PowerShell
text:
First-time setup on Windows PowerShell
Use an admin-scoped token from the BitCadence installation, **not** an ordinary
worker token. The usual local token is `MCO_LOCAL_TOKEN` in the
installation's `.env` or `~/.mco/.env`; do not paste it into logs or a ticket.
The dedicated Jev credential is stored in the server-side encrypted vault.
Run the following in one PowerShell session, with the gateway already running:
$adminSecret = Read-Host 'BitCadence operator token' -AsSecureString
$typesafeSecret = Read-Host 'TypeSafe API key' -AsSecureString
$adminToken = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', $adminSecret).Password
$typesafeKey = [System.Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', $typesafeSecret).Password
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $adminToken" }
$body = @{ mode = 'shadow'; model = 'jev-latest'; api_key = $typesafeKey } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:18789/api/jev' -Headers $headers -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $body
Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:18789/api/jev/test' -Headers $headers
Remove-Variable adminSecret, typesafeSecret, adminToken, typesafeKey, headers, body -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

The test response should report `configured: true`, `available: true`,
`ok: true`. It tests connectivity/model discovery, not a live Jev judgment;
`live_invocation: false` is expected in shadow mode. An `Invalid or missing
agent token` response (401) means the bearer value is absent, wrong, or not
accepted by this gateway. A 403 means the token is valid but lacks the `admin`
scope. An admin-scoped agent token is accepted by this Jev configuration API;
Score's human-only grant endpoints are a separate, stricter boundary.
The Admin Console's generic settings expose mode/model fields, but the
credential and explicit connection test currently use this API; there is no
dedicated Jev key form yet. This is a product gap, not a reason to put the key
in client-side code.
To stop future Jev requests, set `mode` to `disabled` through the same admin
endpoint. Disabling does not erase the encrypted key.

title: DecisionReceipt
BitCadence effects boundary
text:
BitCadence effects boundary
No current BitCadence Score capability lets Jev create grants, approve
checkpoints, or execute cloud/repository effects. Any future `typesafe:invoke`
Score adapter requires its own digest-bound grant, budget, effect receipt, and
adversarial review before live use.

title: J03 shadow operations
text:
J03 shadow operations
BitCadence paths may ask Jev for an annotation after deterministic code
has already produced an outcome. Even if the global mode is `assist` or
`active`, these paths treat Jev as annotation-only: `applied` is always false,
and no Jev answer mutates durable truth or authorizes an effect.
Use case
Question set
What Jev may suggest
What code still owns
`drumline-ops` v1
kind, inject, contradiction, staleness, sensitivity, relevance
Classify completed output; flag recall quality
Stored kind (`fact` / `decision` / `lesson` / `handoff` / `artifact`), content, weight, tags, recall order. `incident` is annotation-only and is not a Drumline kind. `inject=skip` cannot prevent `remember()`.
`watchdog-symptom` v1
action (`retry` / `reroute` / `escalate` / `operator-review` / `noise`)
Classify an already-computed delivery step
Stall timers, max reroutes, reroute CAS, crash-loop safeguards, chain-stall detection, kill switch, who is rerouted.
`notify-quality` v1
duplicate, urgency, impact
Quality of a push that `_allowed` already admitted
Rate budgets, urgent-bypass, identical-message dedup, the Priority header, and whether the message is sent.
Question sets are frozen and digest-bound. Changing instructions, criteria, or
candidate meanings requires a new version string. DecisionReceipts are appended
as `jev_decision` audit events when a `job_id` is provided and the provider is
not disabled. Persist failure is logged and ignored; receipts are never rewritten.
`jev_decision` events are ignored by the delivery stall clock, so an annotation
cannot postpone rekick, reroute, or escalate. Disabled mode records process-level
metrics only and performs no network request and no audit write, so durable state
matches today's deterministic tests.

title: Codex task routing
text:
Codex task routing
`mco_jev_route` is the Codex-facing MCP tool. It sends the current task and a
bounded context summary to the frozen `codex-task-route` registry. Jev may
describe task kind, semantic complexity, reasoning need, execution shape, and
whether the eventual task packet needs current information, workspace evidence,
acceptance criteria, or a material clarification.
The MCP server forwards this request to the gateway's `POST /api/jev/route`
endpoint using the narrow `jev:route` capability. This keeps the decision on
the tenant's configured SecretVault provider; if the gateway is unavailable,
the MCP tool falls back to the local deterministic route.
Jev does not select spend. Deterministic policy combines those annotations with
verified five-hour and weekly Codex capacity plus a caller-supplied context-
pressure label. The policy recommends Luna, Terra, Sol, or Astra, reasoning
effort, maximum parallelism, and root/subagent/BitCadence/hybrid execution.
Astra is ineligible when capacity is unknown, five-hour remaining is below 30%,
weekly remaining is below 20%, or context pressure is high. Below 15% five-hour
remaining, the policy conserves usage and suppresses parallel subagents.
The result remains advisory (`applied=false`). It cannot switch the already-
running root model, spawn a subagent, or create a BitCadence job. Codex applies
the recommendation through explicit spawn parameters or `mco_send`, preserving
the user's original scope and all existing authority boundaries.

title: Jev routing and its limits
text:
Jev routing and its limits
Jev supplies bounded routing advice. It does not approve work, grant permissions, choose a numeric spend quota, or change your running session's model. Deterministic code and existing human gates retain those decisions.

title: Ask for a Claude Code tier recommendation
text:
Ask for a Claude Code tier recommendation
bitcadence jev route-model --task "Review a documentation change"

**Expected:** JSON describing a suggested Claude Code tier and routing outcome. This particular CLI command suggests a tier such as haiku, sonnet or opus; it is not a universal model picker and does not launch a worker.
Add bounded context and choose the fallback tier when useful:
bitcadence jev route-model --task "Review a documentation change" --context "Only the public user guides changed" --deterministic-tier sonnet

Read the returned **outcome, tier and reason**. An exit code of zero does not prove a model answered: disabled, unconfigured, network and timeout cases can return a deterministic fallback successfully. The default fallback is sonnet. [All options](mco-cli-reference.md#cli-mco-jev-route-model).

title: Configure the provider
text:
Configure the provider
Provider configuration is an administrator task. Follow the [Jev provider setup guide](jev-provider-setup.md) for complete PowerShell instructions and credential handling. The server stores the dedicated API key through its encrypted vault; do not put it in browser code, screenshots or support messages.
Endpoint
Purpose
GET /api/jev
Read sanitized provider metadata, never the secret
PUT /api/jev
Set mode, exact model, timeout, retries and optionally the key using admin authorization
POST /api/jev/test
Test provider model discovery; this can make an external request
There is **no dedicated console task-routing test screen or Jev key form** in this inspected version. Generic settings expose some provider fields, but are not the complete connection procedure. Do not look for the old wiki's “Settings → LLM Connections / Routing” walkthrough; that screen was not implemented in the inspected routes.

title: Understand the modes
text:
Understand the modes
**Disabled:** no provider request; use deterministic behavior.
**Shadow:** evaluate advice without applying it. The moving `jev-latest` alias is for shadow evaluation.
**Assist / active:** require a pinned exact model and still obey the deterministic use-case contract. A mode name does not give the provider permission to execute effects.
Annotation-only paths remain annotation-only even when the global mode is active. A receipt records a judgment, not permission. The [provider contract](jev-provider-setup.md) explains supported use cases, receipts and fallback behavior.

title: Codex task routing
text:
Codex task routing
The agent-facing MCP tool `mco_jev_route` is distinct from the CLI tier recommendation. It accepts the current task, short context, current model, verified five-hour/weekly remaining percentages, and context pressure. Its result can recommend an execution shape and prompt improvements. It cannot switch the already-running root model or override policy, budgets, approvals or grants.
Missing usage is unknown, not zero and not unlimited. A provider failure must not block ordinary work. Preserve the original task and use a clear deterministic fallback.

title: If the recommendation is missing or surprising
text:
If the recommendation is missing or surprising
Read the returned outcome and reason before treating it as a successful provider answer.
Check the provider's sanitized configuration and mode with the administrator procedure above.
If desired and authorized for an external provider request, run the explicit connection test. Passing discovery is not proof of a real judgment or a completed worker task.
Make the task description concrete: target, relevant context, constraints and what completion means. Avoid sending secrets or unnecessary personal data.
Inspect the exact model requested and the model reported by the receipt. Do not substitute a different model silently.
To disable future provider requests, use the documented admin configuration endpoint to set mode to disabled. That does not erase the encrypted key or approve any pending work.

title: Job Board & Managing Tasks
text: Job Board & Managing Tasks

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Submit new tasks to helper dropboxes, inspect real-time queue states, examine tamper-evident execution drawers, and manage task lifecycles (retries, cancellations, reassignments, and archiving).

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Open the Job Board
text:
1. Open the Job Board
In the left menu, click **Job Board**. Its heading reads **All work**.
![Job Board Table View](img/04-console-job-board.png)

title: 2. Filter and Search Tasks
text:
2. Filter and Search Tasks
Use the tabs at the top to focus on one kind of work. Each shows a count:
**All**
**Active:** picked up by a helper and running.
**Needs approval:** paused at a human gate.
**Waiting:** waiting for an earlier step.
**Done**
**Problems:** failed or rejected.
Type in **Search jobs** to filter, pick a role from **All roles**, or change the sort order (the default is **Priority, then oldest**).

title: 3. Creating a New Job
text:
3. Creating a New Job
For most work, [Ask for something](Ask.md) is easier. To drop one job on the board yourself:
Click **+ New job** in the upper right.
Fill out the panel:
**What needs to happen?** A plain-English summary (for example, *"Summarize repository changes"*).
**Details:** anything the helper should know. It reads this.
**Who should do it?** Pick a role: `claude`, `codex`, `antigravity` and so on.
**Ask me before it runs:** tick this if the job must pause for your approval first.
**Retry budget:** how many automatic retries if the helper fails.
**Escalate to role:** where it goes when retries run out.
![New Job Creation Composer](img/14-job-create-modal.png)
Click **Create job**. The task appears on the Job Board.

title: 4. Inspecting Job Details & History
text:
4. Inspecting Job Details & History
Click any job row. The job panel slides in from the right:
**Header:** the status word and the job title.
**Change this job:** the actions that make sense for its state (see below).
**Assigned to / Requested by / Created / Job ID.**
**History:** an append-only timeline: created, picked up, completed or failed, and so on.
![Job Detail Drawer and History](img/15-job-detail-drawer.png)

title: 5. Managing Job Actions
text:
5. Managing Job Actions
Under **Change this job**, depending on the job's state:
**Approve / Reject:** when the job needs your OK. See [Approvals](Approvals.md).
**Retry:** puts a failed or rejected job back in line.
**Reassign…:** copies the job to a different role and archives the original.
**Call it off…:** stops an in-flight or waiting job.
**Archive / Unarchive:** hides finished work without deleting its history.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
Every Job Board action maps directly to the `mco` command-line tool:
# Drop a new job into a helper's inbox
mco send codex `
  --title "Summarize the repository" `
  --message "Review recent commits on main and summarize changes." `
  --approve

# Inspect tamper-evident audit history
mco audit <job-id>

# Check for duplicate tasks
mco duplicates <job-id>

# Retry a failed job
mco retry <job-id>

# Cancel a job
mco cancel <job-id>

# Reassign a job to a different role
mco reassign <job-id> --to-role claude

# Archive a completed job
mco archive <job-id>

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Atomic Leases:** When a worker picks up a job, the status changes from `pending` to `leased` / `in_progress`. The table stamps `leased_by_instance_id` with the worker's unique ID.
**Tamper-Evident History:** The audit trail shows every transition with the exact actor ID and UTC timestamp. The database prohibits updating or deleting historical event rows.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Job stuck in 'waiting' status"
text:
1. "Job stuck in 'waiting' status"
**Cause:** The job has dependencies (`depends_on`) that have not yet reached `completed`.
**Fix:** Open the Job Detail Drawer, check the **Depends on** field, and ensure the parent job finishes successfully.

title: 2. "Job stuck in 'needs_approval' status"
text:
2. "Job stuck in 'needs_approval' status"
**Cause:** The job was created with governance enabled and is paused at a human gate.
**Fix:** Go to the **Approval Queue**, review the instructions, and click **Approve**.

title: 3. "Job immediately fails with 'S3 / Network / Tool error'"
text:
3. "Job immediately fails with 'S3 / Network / Tool error'"
**Cause:** The helper crashed or encountered an unhandled exception during execution.
**Fix:** Inspect the error message in the job panel. If transient, click **Retry**. If the assigned role cannot handle the task, click **Reassign** to route to another role.

title: Complete CLI reference
text:
Complete CLI reference
Use `bitcadence` for everyday work. `mco` is a supported compatibility name for the **same command tree**: every path below works with either executable. The desktop entry point is separate: `bitcadence-desktop` launches the native desktop app; its pages are covered by the [GUI reference](gui-reference.md).
This reference covers every registered command and group recursively, every positional argument, option spelling, parser default, repeatable/variadic parameter, prompt and declared range/path constraint. It includes generated completion/help options and the hidden compatibility option `gui --flow`. Defaults are parser defaults; configuration or the implementation may resolve unset values at runtime. `~` means your home directory; `.mco`, `MCO_` and the Python package `mco` remain supported compatibility names.

title: Read this first
text:
Read this first
Run `bitcadence` in an interactive terminal for the menu. In scripts/non-interactive use it prints help and exits 2; `bitcadence --no-menu` deliberately prints help and exits 0. `MCO_NO_MENU=1` also disables the menu.
Put global options before the command: `bitcadence --debug status`. Group options belong before their subcommand, for example `bitcadence helpers --json`.
Add `--help` to a specific command to inspect it safely, for example `bitcadence score start --help`. Except for the transparent `advanced` forwarder, help exits before operational callbacks. No credentials or production commands were executed to produce this reference.
Examples containing JOB_ID, INSTANCE_ID, WORKER_NAME, SCHEDULE_NAME, EXCHANGE_ID, CLIENT_WORKTREE, or file names require your actual values/files. They describe intended operations; they are not a script to run from top to bottom. Commands that change state say so in their expected result/recovery notes. For effectful/restricted operations the example may intentionally stop at help.
`--yes` only exists where listed. It skips that command's questions; it does not add permission. A daemon running, a job submitted, or an exit-0 policy reply does not prove the work succeeded.
Most failures exit 1; syntax errors typically exit 2. Important exceptions are documented per command (empty results/missing schedule or fleet config/advisory verdicts). Do not infer success from exit code alone.

title: Find a command
text:
Find a command
[mco advanced](#cli-mco-advanced) — Run any original command, e.g. `bitcadence advanced audit <job-id>`.
[mco agents](#cli-mco-agents) — List all registered agents and their current online presence status.
[mco approve](#cli-mco-approve) — Approve what's waiting for you, one at a time.
[mco archive](#cli-mco-archive) — Archive a completed/failed/rejected/cancelled job (reversible).
[mco ask](#cli-mco-ask) — Say what you want done. You see the plan and OK it before anything runs.
[mco audit](#cli-mco-audit) — Print a job's tamper-evident audit trail (oldest event first).
[mco audit-checkpoint](#cli-mco-audit-checkpoint) — Export a signed checkpoint. Keep it outside the database/backup volume.
[mco cancel](#cli-mco-cancel) — Call off a job that hasn't finished yet (approver-role token).
[mco cio](#cli-mco-cio) — Deterministic policy checks backing ops/cio-sidecar-brief.md.
[mco cio check](#cli-mco-cio-check) — Check one proposal against the brief's mechanical rules and print a verdict.
[mco connect](#cli-mco-connect) — Connect an AI app to BitCadence.
[mco connectors](#cli-mco-connectors) — List configured enterprise connectors and their health (via the gateway).
[mco deregister](#cli-mco-deregister) — Remove an agent registration. Its token stops working immediately.

title: Shared recovery
text: Shared recovery For gateway/credential failures, inspect `bitcadence status --details` and `bitcadence doctor`; check the configured gateway and the exact caller identity. title: mco launch
text: `mco launch` Fire a launcher right now, by name. Usage example: `bitcadence launch LAUNCHER_NAME` **Expected result:** Runs a named launcher immediately through the scheduled-launch code path; job launchers print job IDs, while local app/URL launchers act locally and queue nothing. **If it fails / before changing state:** Uses ~/.mco/schedules.yaml. Missing config or an unknown launcher produces guidance; --approve/--no-approve override the launcher's approval gate. Launching can create real jobs or open local applications even when done as a manual test. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:1157](../../src/mco/cli.py#L1157). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). title: mco listen
text: `mco listen` Spawn the background daemon client that polls and executes Job Board tasks. Usage example: `bitcadence listen --role codex --instance demo-worker --config-file agent_config.json` **Expected result:** Starts the polling/execution listener for the selected role and identity in the current process. **If it fails / before changing state:** This is an executor, not a passive status monitor. Supply the correct agent config and credential. Use the exact identity you intend to claim work; stop with Ctrl+C. A caught critical listener error is printed without an explicit nonzero exit, so inspect the output as well as the process status. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:1933](../../src/mco/cli.py#L1933). title: mco register

The implementation upserts by instance ID: reusing a name replaces that registration's token, role and supplied fields. **If it fails / before changing state:** Use helpers add for the everyday guided path and choose a distinct identity per helper. Unknown organizations/scopes are rejected. On an older database without a scopes column, registration can fall back to role-derived scopes with an explicit migration warning; inspect the output before assuming the requested scope restriction was stored. text: `mco reset-token` Rotate an agent's access token. The old token stops working immediately. Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `KEY` (positional) TEXT; optional not set Setting key to read or write (blank = list all). `VALUE` (positional) TEXT; optional not set New value for the key (omit with --unset to clear). `--unset` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Clear the key back to its default. `--show-advanced` / `--all` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Show every setting, the address and the masked sign-in. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco setup
text: `mco setup` Configure BitCadence - a guided walkthrough or a jump-anywhere settings menu. Usage example: `bitcadence setup` **Expected result:** Opens the configuration walkthrough/menu. --guided requests the complete walkthrough; --menu jumps straight to settings. **If it fails / before changing state:** Can save configuration and credentials. Follow the selected path and then run doctor to find any remaining installation problem. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:106](../../src/mco/cli.py#L106). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--guided` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Run the full guided walkthrough. `--menu` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Jump straight to the settings menu. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco start
text: `mco start` Start BitCadence quietly in the background (the pair of 'mco stop'). Usage example: `bitcadence start --no-open` **Expected result:** Starts the gateway hidden in the background, using ~/.mco/logs/gateway.log. Normally also opens the signed-in app, ensures a status icon and registers login startup on the first run. **If it fails / before changing state:** Use status and inspect the log if it does not come up. --no-open suppresses browser opening (the tray is still ensured); --no-autostart suppresses first-run login startup registration. stop is the paired shutdown command. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:730](../../src/mco/cli.py#L730). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--host` TEXT; optional `127.0.0.1` The host to bind to. `--port` INTEGER; optional `18789` The port to bind to. `--no-open` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Don't open the app in the browser. `--no-autostart` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Don't set BitCadence to start when you sign in. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco status
text: `mco status` Plain summary: what needs you, what's running, any problems. Usage example: `bitcadence status --details` **Expected result:** Without flags, prints a plain summary of waiting/running/problem work. --details returns technical diagnostics; --json is for the plain summary path. **If it fails / before changing state:** --all includes all resolved configuration keys, including unrelated process environment, and selects diagnostics. --json does not make --details/--all JSON. Review diagnostics before sharing; process health alone does not establish work completion. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:1984](../../src/mco/cli.py#L1984). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--details` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Show the technical diagnostics (database path, profile, settings). `--all` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Show all resolved configuration keys, including unrelated process environment. `--json` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Machine-readable summary. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco stop
text: `mco stop` Stop a running BitCadence gateway (by port). Safe inspection example (prints help only): `bitcadence stop --help` **Operation result (when run with the required values):** Finds listening processes by port and terminates them without asking. Normally waits five seconds before escalating to a kill; --force kills immediately. **If it fails / before changing state:** Inspect the port and intended process first: the implementation targets listeners on that port, not a verified BitCadence process identity. No listener is a normal exit-0 result. This does not cancel queued jobs or remove service registration. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:1856](../../src/mco/cli.py#L1856). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--port` INTEGER; optional `18789` Port the gateway is running on. `--force` / `-f` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Send SIGKILL immediately instead of graceful SIGTERM. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco sync
text: `mco sync` Pull open platform objects (incidents/problems) onto the job board. Usage example: `bitcadence sync servicenow` **Expected result:** Pulls open external incidents/problems into the job board and prints pulled/created/skipped counts. **If it fails / before changing state:** This creates board work. Run connectors first to check configured names/health. Existing imported objects are skipped rather than all recreated. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:3372](../../src/mco/cli.py#L3372). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `CONNECTOR` (positional) TEXT; required required Connector name (servicenow, dynatrace). `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco tail
text: `mco tail` Live-tail a filtered mailbox feed from the gateway broadcast socket. Usage example: `bitcadence tail --role codex --instance demo-worker` **Expected result:** Streams broadcast job events filtered by target role and instance; Ctrl+C stops the stream. **If it fails / before changing state:** Uses configured identity/gateway/token when flags are absent. Authentication failure prints guidance; disconnections retry with backoff. An empty feed does not prove an empty inbox. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:3229](../../src/mco/cli.py#L3229). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--role` TEXT; optional not set Agent role mailbox to tail. `--instance` TEXT; optional not set Agent instance mailbox to tail. `--gateway` TEXT; optional not set Gateway HTTP URL. `--token` TEXT; optional not set Agent or operator bearer token. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco tray
text: `mco tray` Status light and a door into the console (Windows tray / macOS menu bar / Linux AppIndicator). Safe inspection example (prints help only): `bitcadence tray --help` **Operation result (when run with the required values):** Runs the optional system status light/console doorway. --daemon starts it hidden where supported. **If it fails / before changing state:** Needs the tray desktop dependencies and a usable desktop session. This is an interface, not the gateway or an executor. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:1140](../../src/mco/cli.py#L1140). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--daemon` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` The advanced tray that drives the worker daemon. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco unarchive
text: `mco unarchive` Undo archive. Usage example: `bitcadence unarchive JOB_ID` **Expected result:** Makes an archived job visible again in the default board view. **If it fails / before changing state:** Does not retry or reopen the job. Use audit/status to inspect its existing terminal result. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:2763](../../src/mco/cli.py#L2763). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `JOB_ID` (positional) TEXT; required required Archived job ID to restore to the default board view. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco upgrade
text: `mco upgrade` Apply schema migrations to the configured backend. Usage example: `bitcadence upgrade` **Expected result:** Checks schema upgrade requirements. Local SQLite needs no such migrations; supported Postgres/Supabase execution requires --apply. **If it fails / before changing state:** Without --apply, prints pending migration SQL/instructions rather than applying it. Where automatic execution is unavailable, writes a combined script for the Supabase SQL editor. Review output before applying schema changes. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:2044](../../src/mco/cli.py#L2044). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--apply` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Actually apply (default: dry-run / show pending). `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco wake
text: `mco wake` Wake a local worker command when this agent's inbox has pending jobs. Safe inspection example (prints help only): `bitcadence wake --help` **Operation result (when run with the required values):** Waits for pending work, then starts the configured local worker shell command, enforcing a minimum interval between starts and optional periodic inbox rechecks. **If it fails / before changing state:** Requires --exec and the exact agent identity/credential. Missing or invalid per-instance credentials fail explicitly instead of silently borrowing the operator credential. Ctrl+C stops the waker; starting an executor is not a job lease/completion proof. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:3302](../../src/mco/cli.py#L3302). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--exec` TEXT; required required Shell command to run when this worker has pending jobs. `--role` TEXT; optional not set Agent role to watch for. `--instance` TEXT; optional not set Agent instance ID to watch for. `--gateway` TEXT; optional not set Gateway HTTP URL. `--token` TEXT; optional not set Agent bearer token. `--min-interval` FLOAT; optional `10.0` Minimum seconds between spawn starts. `--repoll-interval` FLOAT; optional `300.0` Seconds between timer re-checks of the inbox (0 disables). `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco watch
text: `mco watch` Live-tail job events from the gateway's broadcast feed (Ctrl-C to stop). Usage example: `bitcadence watch` **Expected result:** Streams formatted job events; --raw emits raw JSON messages. Reconnects with exponential backoff up to 30 seconds. **If it fails / before changing state:** Ctrl+C stops watching. Authentication failures require the configured MCO_AGENT_TOKEN/MCO_LOCAL_TOKEN to be fixed. This is a live stream, not a replay of all historical events. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:3128](../../src/mco/cli.py#L3128). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `--raw` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Print raw event JSON instead of formatted lines. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.

title: mco workflow
text: `mco workflow` Submit a declarative YAML workflow (DAG of jobs) to the Job Board. Usage example: `bitcadence workflow plan.yaml --dry-run` **Expected result:** Loads YAML, validates the dependency graph and prints the ordered plan. --dry-run prevents submission. **If it fails / before changing state:** Without --dry-run, creates real jobs and prints step-to-job IDs. Correct invalid files/dependencies first. Use the printed IDs to follow outcomes; submission alone is not workflow completion. Implementation: [src/mco/cli.py:2528](../../src/mco/cli.py#L2528). Global/group options: [mco](#cli-mco). Argument / option Type and requirement Default Meaning / constraints `FILE` (positional) TEXT; required required Path to a workflow YAML file. `--dry-run` BOOLEAN; flag; optional `false` Validate and print the plan without submitting. `--help` BOOLEAN; flag; optional not set Show this message and exit.
