title: Home (Overview)
text: Home (Overview)

title: Goal
text:
Goal
See what needs you and what is running from one screen, without reading a job list. Home replaced the old Overview and its metric cards.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Open Home
text:
1. Open Home
Click **Home** at the top of the left menu. It is the first page the console opens.
![BitCadence Home](img/01-console-overview.png)

title: 2. Read "What needs you"
text:
2. Read "What needs you"
This comes first. Each card is one thing waiting on a person, with a count beside the heading:
**Needs you:** a job paused for your approval. Click **Approve** to say yes, or **Look first** to read the details.
**Stuck:** work that failed or has gone quiet. Click **Look first**.

title: 3. Read "What's running"
text:
3. Read "What's running"
Below that, each card is one piece of work in flight, with a state word (**Working**, **Waiting**) and a plain sentence such as *Waiting for a free helper* or *claude is working on this step*. Steps of the same plan are grouped, and a Score run shows as one card. Click a card for more. **See all work** opens the job board.
Home refreshes by itself and shows recent work only. See [Console Home](Console-home.md) for the exact rules, including when a job is called **Stuck**.

title: 4. Look at the rest of the menu
text:
4. Look at the rest of the menu
The left menu also has [Portfolio](gui-reference.md#portfolio), the [Job Board](job-board-and-tasks.md), [Approvals](Approvals.md), Governance, [Ask for something](Ask.md), [Helpers](Helpers.md), [Connect an AI](Connect-an-AI.md), [Schedules](Schedules.md), Drumline, **Activity** and [Settings](Settings.md). **Activity** shows every step every helper took, newest first, with event, failure and helper counts.
![Activity](img/10-console-activity-audit.png)

title: 5. The minimal dashboard
text:
5. The minimal dashboard
`/dashboard` is a smaller, plainer page for a quick look. It asks for a token first, and still uses the technical labels (Operations, Agents & Tokens).
![Minimal dashboard](img/13-minimal-dashboard.png)

title: 6. Advanced mode
text:
6. Advanced mode
The **Advanced** switch in the top bar shows the technical layer (raw IDs, payloads, retry budgets). Leave it off for plain wording.

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
To obtain a quick operational snapshot from your terminal:
# Health check and diagnostic summary
mco status

# List all helpers and their online presence
mco agents

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Live updates:** Cards move between **What needs you** and **What's running** as helpers pick up and finish jobs.
**Failure alerts:** A job that fails with no retries left appears under **What needs you** as **Stuck**.
**Demo mode:** Before you connect, the bottom of the left menu says **Demo · simulated data** and the cards are examples.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Home looks out of date"
text:
1. "Home looks out of date"
**Cause:** The connection to the gateway was interrupted.
**Fix:** Check the status at the bottom of the left menu: it should say **Live**. If it does not, refresh the browser page (`F5`).

title: 2. "No helpers are working"
text:
2. "No helpers are working"
**Cause:** No background helpers or daemon listeners are running.
**Fix:** Start helpers in the Desktop Manager, or launch a listener from a terminal:
mco listen --role codex --instance worker-1

title: Projects Dashboard
text:
Projects Dashboard
**Note:** The console sidebar now opens **Portfolio** (see [Portfolio](gui-reference.md#portfolio)) in place of the **Projects** page described below. The earlier project grouping view is no longer reachable from the sidebar. The project metadata, assignment and API details on this page still describe how jobs are tagged with a project.

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Group disparate helper tasks into cohesive business projects and initiatives, observe project-level health and completion velocity, and detect blocked or stalled initiatives.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Navigate to Projects
text:
1. Navigate to Projects
In the left menu, click **Projects**.
![Projects Dashboard Overview](img/03-console-projects.png)

title: 2. Inspect Project Groups
text:
2. Inspect Project Groups
**Projects at a glance** groups jobs by their `input_payload.project` or workflow (for example `gateway-reliability` or `release-2.4`). Work with neither stays visible under **Unassigned work**, so nothing silently disappears.
The three cards at the top show **Open projects**, **Need you** (decisions or problems) and **Jobs complete**.
Use **Open**, **Needs attention** and **All** to choose which projects to list, or search by project or job name.
Each project card shows:
**A state word:** for example **Needs your OK**.
**A progress bar:** how many jobs are done (for example 3/9).
**Next action:** the one thing to do next.
**Its jobs,** each with a status word and a **Move** button to put it in another project.

title: 3. Filter Jobs by Project
text:
3. Filter Jobs by Project
Click **Open Job Board** to see every job in the table.

title: 4. Assigning a Job to a Project
The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
You can inspect and assign projects from the command line:
# Assign an existing job to a project
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18789/api/jobs/<job-id>/project `
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $env:MCO_AGENT_TOKEN" `
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" `
  -d '{"project": "gateway-reliability"}'

# Fetch project-level aggregate view
curl http://127.0.0.1:18789/api/jobs/project-view `
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $env:MCO_AGENT_TOKEN"

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**High-Level Rollup:** Instead of scrolling through hundreds of granular helper tasks, you see 3–5 top-level project initiatives.
**Coverage Summary:** The top header displays total managed project tasks, active count, and whether coverage is truncated (up to 5,000 tasks evaluated server-side).

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Jobs appear in 'Uncategorized' project"
text:
1. "Jobs appear in 'Uncategorized' project"
**Cause:** Jobs were created without a `project` key in their `input_payload`.
**Fix:** Add `"project": "my-project-name"` to the job creation payload or workflow YAML definition.

title: 2. "Project marked as Blocked"
text:
2. "Project marked as Blocked"
**Cause:** A prerequisite job in a workflow failed or was rejected, stopping downstream dependent tasks.
**Fix:** Click the project card to view the jobs, open the failed job, and either click **Retry** or **Reassign** to clear the block.

title: From installed to your first result
text:
From installed to your first result
**Goal:** complete one small, low-risk task and know where to find its result.

title: Before you begin
page: From installed to your first result
text:
Before you begin
Follow the [install guide](install-first-run.md). You need a running gateway, a connected console, and a helper configured to accept the role you choose. Setup screens do not buy model credits or make an unavailable provider start working.

title: Start and check
page: From installed to your first result
text:
Start and check
bitcadence start
bitcadence status
bitcadence helpers
mco gui

**Expected:** the console opens. If it shows **Demo**, [connect to the gateway](connecting-console.md) before submitting real work. An online helper is a useful signal; the proof is a completed task with a recorded result.

title: Submit a small task
page: From installed to your first result
text:
Submit a small task
Choose **Ask for something**.
Describe a bounded task, such as “Summarize the README and suggest three clearer headings.” Choose files your helper can access.
Choose **Draft a plan** and read each step. The planner uses predictable sentence rules, not a full understanding of your intent.
Remove unwanted steps or change the request and draft again. Add a final approval where you need a decision.
Choose **Approve and start** when the plan matches your intent.
Find the task on **Home** or **Job board** and open its details.
[Ask for something](Ask.md) covers repeats, conditional steps and the CLI equivalent. A saved YAML plan submitted with `--file` is real execution, not a preview. The text-based CLI Ask path still requires its first job to be approved after the initial plan confirmation, including with `--yes`.

title: Know when you are done
page: From installed to your first result
text:
Know when you are done
Look for a terminal success state **and** the recorded result or handoff. Open the referenced output. A green light or an empty queue alone does not prove the work was completed.
For waiting decisions, use [Approvals](Approvals.md). If no worker takes a job, check its role/instance, helper credentials and worker process in [worker setup](workers-and-daemon-listening.md). Understand a failure before retrying; avoid duplicate jobs.

title: If you get stuck
page: From installed to your first result
text:
If you get stuck
bitcadence status --details
bitcadence fix

**Expected:** details describe the problem; Fix offers repairs. Read each repair before accepting it. Avoid `--yes` while learning the workflow.
The [pause guide](approvals-and-governance.md) explains execution controls. Pausing can halt active attempts. Inspect affected jobs before retrying an interrupted action.

title: Schedules
text:
Schedules
Open `/console` and choose **Schedules**, or run `bitcadence schedule` in a
terminal. Both show each schedule as a sentence, such as **Every weekday at
2:00 AM**, with when it runs next and an On/Off switch. No file is ever shown.

title: Add one
text:
Add one
Pick what should run, how often (Every day, Every weekday, Certain days, Every
hour) and the time. The sentence you will get is shown before you save. Your time
zone is detected from your computer.
bitcadence schedule
bitcadence schedule add
bitcadence schedule add --what "Nightly dependency audit" --when "every weekday at 2 AM"
bitcadence schedule off "Nightly dependency"
bitcadence schedule on "Nightly dependency"

`--when` takes plain words: `every day at 7 am`, `every weekday at 2 AM`,
`every Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 9:15 pm`, `every hour`. A time without AM
or PM is asked about, not guessed. Words that cannot be understood get one
sentence back and nothing is saved:
I didn't understand "every second tuesday". Try "every weekday at 2 AM".

`--yes` saves without asking.

title: What is behind it
text:
What is behind it
The choices are written to `~/.mco/schedules.yaml`, the same file the original
`mco schedule` commands use (`init`, `list`, `enable`, `disable`, `reset`, `tick`,
`run` all still work). A new schedule is appended as text, so comments in a file
you edited by hand are kept, and the result is read back before it is saved. Only
things already defined as work to run can be scheduled; open-a-page and
open-an-app entries are not offered.
The console uses `GET /api/schedules`, `POST /api/schedules/preview`, `POST
/api/schedules` and `POST /api/schedules/{id}/enabled`. Reading needs `jobs:read`;
adding or switching one needs `agents:manage`.

title: Scheduling & Recurring Loops
text: Scheduling & Recurring Loops

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Automate recurring helper tasks on timers, cron schedules, or bounded iteration loops, ensuring all periodic runs inherit full governance, approval gates, and audit trails.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: The easy way: the Schedules page
text:
The easy way: the Schedules page
In the console, click **Schedules**. Each saved schedule is a card with its name, when it runs (for example *Every day at 2:00 AM*), the next run, and an **On** switch. To add one, use **New schedule**: choose what should run, how often (**Every day**, **Every weekday**, **Certain days** or **Every hour**) and the time. The sentence at the bottom shows exactly what you are saving. See [Schedules](Schedules.md). To make something repeat straight from a request, use **Make it repeat** on [Ask for something](Ask.md).
![Schedules](img/23-console-schedules.png)
The rest of this page covers the file behind it, for launchers, cron and loops.

title: 1. Initialize Scheduling Configuration
text:
1. Initialize Scheduling Configuration
Generate the default schedules file in your user home:
mco schedule init

This creates `~/.mco/schedules.yaml`.

title: 2. Configure Launchers and Loops
text:
2. Configure Launchers and Loops
Open `~/.mco/schedules.yaml` in your text editor:
# Reusable launch templates
launchers:
  nightly-audit:
    role: reviewer
    title: Nightly dependency vulnerability audit
    instructions: Scan dependency lockfiles for known CVEs.
    requires_approval: false
    max_retries: 2
    escalate_to_role: human

  release-check:
    workflow: workflows/release-pipeline.yaml

# Timing and trigger loops
schedules:
  audit-cron:
    launcher: nightly-audit
    cron: "0 2 * * *"            # Runs every night at 02:00 UTC
    enabled: true

  health-pulse:
    launcher: nightly-audit
    interval_seconds: 3600       # Runs every hour
    max_iterations: 24           # Bounded loop: stops after 24 runs
    enabled: true

title: 3. Inspecting and Testing Schedules
text:
3. Inspecting and Testing Schedules
List all active schedules and their next fire timestamps:
mco schedule list

Test-fire a launcher manually to verify the prompt without waiting for cron:
mco launch nightly-audit

Run a dry run to simulate the next tick:
mco schedule tick --dry-run

title: 4. Running the Scheduler Engine
text:
4. Running the Scheduler Engine
Run the scheduler in the foreground:
mco schedule run

Or install it as a persistent OS service:
mco service install-scheduler

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
Manage individual scheduled loops without rewriting YAML:
# Disable a schedule temporarily
mco schedule disable audit-cron

# Re-enable a paused schedule
mco schedule enable audit-cron

# Reset iteration history for a completed loop
mco schedule reset health-pulse

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Governed Origin Stamps:** When a scheduled job is created on the Job Board, its metadata contains:
Origin: loop: audit-cron #12

**Audit Trails:** You can look back months later and see exactly which schedule authorized each job, which helper leased it, and what was produced.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Invalid cron expression"
text:
1. "Invalid cron expression"
**Cause:** Non-standard cron syntax.
**Fix:** Use standard 5-part cron syntax (`minute hour day month day-of-week`).

title: 2. "Schedule marked completed and stops running"
text:
2. "Schedule marked completed and stops running"
**Cause:** The schedule reached its configured `max_iterations` limit.
**Fix:** Run `mco schedule reset <name>` to clear the iteration counter, or remove `max_iterations` for infinite execution.

title: Live Score
text:
Live Score
From Home, tap a running Score card. **Back to Home** returns to the overview.
This drawing is read-only: it cannot edit the plan, approve work, retry a job,
pause a run, or create jobs.
Stages come from the stored run definition, including tasks that have not yet
been dispatched. Work and review cards come from that run's dispatch records.
Rejection paths appear as **Repeats with … if changes are needed**, and each
card labels its work/review round. Worker progress stays visible. **See more**
reveals the job identifier. Columns scroll sideways on a phone.
The console reads `/api/score/autonomy/runs/{run_id}` every ten seconds while
this view is open. This authenticated `jobs:read` endpoint is on the existing
Score status router. It checks the caller's organization and uses a read-only
SQLite connection, returning only drawing fields. It reads at most 200 matching
job rows from the gateway board. Larger runs still show all planned stages and
show a notice that some job details are outside the view. If a job row is not
available, the card uses its dispatch state rather than inventing progress.
The endpoint is a synchronous FastAPI handler so database work runs in the
worker pool. Reading it does not open a writable conductor or tick the run.
Missing runs and runs in another organization return the same unavailable
response. Connection/read failures show a plain error; a stale plan is not
silently presented as current.
Home and this drawing share the ten-minute silence setting described in
[Home](Console-home.md). A recent heartbeat counts as a sign of life even while a long
operation has not produced a new progress sentence. A stall changes only the
display label, not the actual job state.

title: Autonomous Scores & Conductor
text: Autonomous Scores & Conductor

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Author, validate, and monitor **Scores** — versioned, deterministic JSON contracts that coordinate long-running autonomous development and operations runs with cryptographic evidence, resource locks, and policy gates.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. What is a Score?
text:
1. What is a Score?
Unlike simple jobs or legacy workflows, a **Score** is an immutable, digest-bound contract that defines:
The complete goal hierarchy and dependency graph.
Required worker capabilities and role boundaries (independent authors and reviewers).
Resource locks (such as isolated repository worktrees or deployment lanes).
Mandatory test evidence and verification receipts.
Explicit human checkpoints and integer-cent budget limits.

title: 2. Watching Score Runs in the Console
text:
2. Watching Score Runs in the Console
Open **Home**. Each Score run appears under **What's running** as one card per run, with a state word, a sentence from the worker's progress and the step count from the real plan.
Tap a Score card to watch its read-only live drawing.
See [Console Home](Console-home.md) and [Live Score](Score-live.md) for what the cards and the drawing show. The older **Live look** window on the Overview screen no longer exists.

title: 3. Validating and Compiling Scores Offline
text:
3. Validating and Compiling Scores Offline
Before submitting any score, validate and compile it locally using the offline kernel:
# 1. Validate score structure against JSON Schema
python -m mco.orchestrator.scores validate examples\scores\via-cloud.score.json

# 2. Compile score into deterministic, digest-bound work packets
python -m mco.orchestrator.scores compile examples\scores\via-cloud.score.json

# 3. Preview planned tasks, dependencies, and capability requirements
python -m mco.orchestrator.scores preview examples\scores\via-cloud.score.json

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
Manage and advance Score Conductor runs from PowerShell:
# Check status of conductor and active score runs
mco score status --run-id <run-id>

# List the runs in the conductor database
mco score list

# Advance the conductor sweep engine
mco score tick --run-id <run-id>

# Grant local development policy authority
mco score grant-local examples/scores/via-cloud.score.json --run-id <run-id> --action <action> --resource <resource>

To approve a reusable Score class once for unattended local runs, with immediate revocation, see [Standing Score grants](standing-score-grants.md).

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Independent Review Enforced:** A worker cannot approve its own work. If `codex-build-1` authors a change, the Conductor requires an independent reviewer (`reviewer-beast` or `gemini-qa-1`) before the task is accepted.
**Worker Completion ≠ Task Acceptance:** A worker returning `completed` does not advance the score. Only verified evidence artifacts and independent review receipts unlock downstream tasks.
**Evidence Binding:** Every event is tied to the score document digest (SHA-256) and run ID, guaranteeing that changing a score contract invalidates previously issued approvals.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Score validation error: Cyclic dependency"
text:
1. "Score validation error: Cyclic dependency"
**Cause:** One goal packet depends on another in a circular loop.
**Fix:** Run `scores validate` to see the exact cycle path reported by the validator.

title: 2. "Score run paused at human checkpoint"
text:
2. "Score run paused at human checkpoint"
**Cause:** The score reached a stage with `checkpoint: true` requiring explicit owner authorization.
**Fix:** Open the Governance or Approvals panel to sign off on the checkpoint decision.

title: 3. "Budget reservation exceeded"
text:
3. "Budget reservation exceeded"
**Cause:** Planned tasks request more compute or token expenditure than the authorized integer-cent limit (`authorized_budget_cents`).
**Fix:** Issue an updated grant with higher budget limits using `mco score grant-local`.

text:
3. Installing OS Services
To survive system restarts and user logouts, install BitCadence components as native OS services:

title: Sidecars & Autonomous Fleet Daemons
text: Sidecars & Autonomous Fleet Daemons

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Understand, install, operate, monitor, and troubleshoot BitCadence background sidecars and worker daemons, including the `claude-cio` Chief sidecar, declarative `fleet.toml` management via `mco fleet apply`, and generic elevated administration.

title: What Sidecars Are (In Plain English)
text:
What Sidecars Are (In Plain English)
In human organizations, high-stakes decisions and dispatch cannot halt simply because an executive steps away from their desk. In BitCadence:
**The Problem:** An interactive AI agent session (such as `claude-desktop` or a developer's IDE session) only runs while the human operator has their computer unlocked and the desktop application running in the foreground. If the operator closes their laptop, locks Windows, or leaves for the evening, the fleet stops: pending approval gates stall, incoming workflow jobs sit unleased in the queue, and background tasks cannot advance.
**The Solution (Sidecars):** A **sidecar** is an always-on, headless background service that runs alongside the primary agent seat or system component. It acts as an autonomous deputy or event-driven waker:
It monitors incoming mail and job queues in SQLite/gateway memory.
It evaluates strict, deterministic policy checks (e.g., verifying spend budgets, forbidden actions, or test requirements).
When the primary interactive seat is offline, it can approve safe, pre-authorized routine actions or queue/escalate high-risk tasks to the human operator.
When tasks addressed to specialized worker roles arrive, event-driven sidecars wake up the corresponding agent runtime on demand.
In BitCadence, sidecars do not bypass governance — they **enforce** governance 24/7 without requiring an open terminal window on your screen.

title: Anatomy of the Fleet: Wakers, Runners, and the CIO
text:
Anatomy of the Fleet: Wakers, Runners, and the CIO
BitCadence distinguishes between three interrelated background concepts:
Component
Role
How It Operates
**Event Waker (`mco wake`)**
The doorbell listener
A lightweight process holding an event connection to the gateway. When a job addressed to its role/instance arrives, it spawns the heavy worker script.
**Worker Runner (`scripts/workers/*`)**
The task executor
The actual shell/PowerShell script (or AI CLI like Codex, Claude, Grok, or Antigravity) that claims the job, checks out a git worktree, runs tests, and submits completion receipts.
**`claude-cio` Sidecar**
The Chief deputy
An always-on sidecar for the fleet's Chief seat. Governed by `ops/cio-sidecar-brief.md`, it evaluates mechanical policies via `mco cio check`, approves safe proposals when `claude-desktop` is offline, and escalates out-of-bounds requests.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. Declarative Fleet Configuration (fleet.toml)
text:
1. Declarative Fleet Configuration (`fleet.toml`)
All background workers and sidecars are configured declaratively in `~/.mco/fleet.toml`. The system supervisor and `mco fleet apply` consult **only** this file.
Sample configuration (`~/.mco/fleet.toml`):
# ============================================================================
# BitCadence Fleet Configuration
# ~/.mco/fleet.toml
# ============================================================================

[workers.claude-cio]
role = "chief"
instance = "claude-cio"
mode = "waker"
exec = "python -m mco.orchestrator.cio_runner"
min_interval = 10
poll_interval = 300
background = true       # Installs as unattended Windows Task (S4U logon)

[workers.codex-worker]
role = "codex"
instance = "codex-beast"
mode = "waker"
exec = "C:/AI/BitCadence/scripts/workers/codex-worker-run.ps1"
min_interval = 10
poll_interval = 1800
background = false      # Runs during active interactive desktop session

[workers.research-poller]
role = "claude"
instance = "claude-research"
mode = "poll"           # Runs on a repeating timer rather than instant wake events
exec = "C:/AI/BitCadence/scripts/workers/claude-worker-run.ps1"
poll_interval = 900     # Runs every 15 minutes

Supported Fields:
`role`: The target mailbox role (`chief`, `codex`, `claude`, `antigravity`, `grok`).
`instance`: The unique instance ID of the worker.
`mode`:
`waker`: Event-driven waker that triggers within seconds of job arrival.
`poll`: Fixed-interval polling loop.
`off`: Configured but disabled; any installed OS service will be uninstalled.
`exec`: Absolute path or executable command line invoked when work arrives.
`min_interval`: Minimum seconds between executions (throttling debounce).
`poll_interval`: Fallback polling interval in seconds.
`background`: (`true`/`false`, default `false`). On Windows, setting to `true` installs the service with `LogonType = S4U`, allowing it to run unattended when the user is logged off. (Requires administrator privileges during installation).

title: 2. Applying Fleet Run Modes (mco fleet apply)
text:
2. Applying Fleet Run Modes (`mco fleet apply`)
To reconcile operating system services or scheduled tasks with your `fleet.toml`:
mco fleet apply

What `mco fleet apply` does:
Validates `~/.mco/fleet.toml` against schema and allowed fields.
Checks for missing agent tokens in `~/.mco/tokens/<instance>.token`. If a token is missing, it prints an upfront warning:
claude-cio: WARNING no token at ~/.mco/tokens/claude-cio.token - the waker will fail to authenticate unless MCO_AGENT_TOKEN is set. Fix: mco reset-token claude-cio

Compares installed OS services against the configuration:
Installs new wakers or polling services.
Updates changed service configurations.
Safely removes services set to `mode = "off"` or omitted from the file.

title: 3. Checking Fleet Status
text:
3. Checking Fleet Status
Query the reconciled state of all declared workers:
mco fleet status

Output displays:
**Worker Name & Instance ID**
**Role**
**Mode (`waker`, `poll`, `off`)**
**Active Service Name** (e.g., `BitCadence-wake-chief-claude-cio`)
**OS Service Status** (`Running`, `Ready`, `Disabled`, or `Not Installed`)
To check live presence reported by the gateway:
mco agents

Inspect `last_seen_seconds` and `connected` status.

title: 4. Stopping and Removing Sidecars
text:
4. Stopping and Removing Sidecars
To stop or remove a sidecar cleanly:
**Via `fleet.toml`:**
Change the worker's mode to `off`:
mco fleet set claude-cio mode=off
mco fleet apply

Or remove the `[workers.claude-cio]` section entirely from `~/.mco/fleet.toml` and run `mco fleet apply`.
**Via `mco service` CLI:**
# Stop a running task immediately (there is no `mco service stop`)
Stop-ScheduledTask -TaskName BitCadence-wake-chief-claude-cio

# Uninstall the scheduled task from the OS
mco service uninstall BitCadence-wake-chief-claude-cio

**Via the Desktop Control Window:**
In the component table, select the worker row.
Click **Stop selected**.
Click **Fleet settings** to edit `fleet.toml`, then click **Reload settings**.

title: 5. The Elevated Admin-Pack Step (Generic Open-Source Guide)
text:
5. The Elevated Admin-Pack Step (Generic Open-Source Guide)
While standard wakers can run in the user's interactive session without administrator privileges, unattended background sidecars (and local CI/CD service runners) require operating system capabilities that standard user accounts cannot grant.
Why Administrator Elevation Is Required on Windows:
**Unattended Execution (`S4U` Logon):** When `background = true` is set, Task Scheduler registers the task with `LogonType = S4U`. Windows requires Administrator elevation to register S4U tasks without storing cleartext passwords.
**Dedicated Service Accounts:** Creating an isolated local user account (e.g., `bc-runner`) to sandbox code execution prevents workers from accessing private personal folders (`%USERPROFILE%\Documents`, SSH keys, or cloud credentials).
**Firewall Binding:** Narrowing local model listening ports (e.g., binding model servers strictly to `127.0.0.1`) requires Windows Advanced Firewall modifications.
Generic Administrator Script Flow:
When setting up elevated services, maintainers use a generic administrator script (e.g., `admin-pack.ps1`). It must follow these strict security principles:
**No Personal Paths:** Uses environment variables (`$env:USERPROFILE`, `$env:ProgramData`, `$PSScriptRoot`) rather than hardcoded developer paths.
**Elevation Check:** Checks for admin rights at startup:
$principal = New-Object Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal([Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent())
if (-not $principal.IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltinRole]::Administrator)) {
    Write-Error "This script must be run as Administrator (right-click PowerShell > Run as administrator)."
    exit 1
}

**Plain-English Confirmation:** Outlines all pending changes and requires typing `YES` before modifying system state.
**Idempotency:** Safe to run repeatedly; skips tasks that are already configured.
**Clean `-Undo` Support:** Allows one-step uninstallation of all services, rules, and accounts:
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\admin-pack.ps1 -Undo

title: Operating the claude-cio Sidecar
text:
Operating the `claude-cio` Sidecar
The `claude-cio` sidecar operates under a formal operating policy defined in `ops/cio-sidecar-brief.md`.

title: Presence & Dual-Mode Behavior
text:
Presence & Dual-Mode Behavior
Before making any decision, `claude-cio` queries `mco_agents`:
                 +-----------------------------------------+
                 |            mco_agents Query             |
                 +-----------------------------------------+
                                      |
                 Is claude-desktop online? (heartbeat < 300s)
                                      |
                      +---------------+---------------+
                      |                               |
                   [ YES ]                         [ NO ]
                      |                               |
             +-----------------+             +-----------------+
             |     Mode A      |             |     Mode B      |
             |   DEFER / CIO   |             |   ACT AS CHIEF  |
             +-----------------+             +-----------------+
             | Posts advisory  |             | Full dispatch   |
             | recommendations |             | authority under |
             | only; leaves    |             | standing policy |
             | binding votes   |             | limits.         |
             | to desktop.     |             |                 |
             +-----------------+             +-----------------+

title: Policy Checks (mco cio check)
text:
Policy Checks (`mco cio check`)
When approving plans, `claude-cio` executes deterministic command-line checks before applying LLM reasoning:
mco cio check --decider claude-cio --project Via --spend-cents 450 --proposed-by codex-beast --category code_review

Hard Standing Policies Enforced:
**Self-Approval Forbidden:** An agent cannot approve its own proposal. Missing, whitespace, or case-mismatched proposer IDs fail closed.
**Project Spend Caps:** Hard monthly limits (e.g., Via: $150, Sim Lab: $25 paper only, Operate: $10). Unrecognized projects or proposals exceeding caps automatically escalate.
**Strict Escalation to Humans:** Requires escalation to human operators for:
Credential or token modifications.
Financial transactions or live broker connections.
Deleting databases or household data.
Bypassing bot protections or CAPTCHAs.

title: How to Know a Sidecar is Healthy or Stuck
text:
How to Know a Sidecar is Healthy or Stuck
Do not rely solely on "Green" or "Online" lights in dashboards. True operational health follows **four distinct verification levels**:
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 1: Supervised Process Exists                                     |
|          OS process or Task Scheduler task is active (PID assigned)    |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 2: Token Authenticates                                           |
|          Gateway accepts credentials without HTTP 401 Unauthorized     |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 3: Leases Pending Work                                           |
|          Pulls jobs from queue when assigned; state changes to leased  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Level 4: Delivers Completed Receipts                                   |
|          Executes instructions, runs tests, posts mco_complete         |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+

title: End-to-End Fleet Smoke Test
text:
End-to-End Fleet Smoke Test
To verify that a sidecar is actually capable of executing work, send an inert, reply-only smoke test:
mco send chief --instance claude-cio --title "FLEET SMOKE TEST - reply only" `
  --message "Do NOT edit files or commit. Call mco_complete(task_id, output) with your AGENT_INSTANCE_ID, the UTC time, and 'fleet smoke ok'. Then stop."

Then follow the job (the job id is printed by `mco send`) in the Job Board or its audit trail:
mco audit <job-id>

Verify the task moves from **`pending`** to **`leased`** and finally **`completed`**.

title: If It Goes Wrong (Real Incident Field Guide)
text: If It Goes Wrong (Real Incident Field Guide)

title: Incident 1: Worker Shows "Online/Standby" but Silently Never Runs (Locked Log File)
text:
Incident 1: Worker Shows "Online/Standby" but Silently Never Runs (Locked Log File)
The Symptom:
The web console and `mco agents` show the worker with a green dot and status `online` or `standby`. Jobs dispatched to the role sit in the queue indefinitely without being leased. No errors appear on the web dashboard.
The Root Cause:
On Windows, file streams use mandatory file sharing locks. If a previous run crashed or a zombie process held an open handle to `~/.mco/logs/<instance>.log` without shared write permissions:
The waker process maintains a healthy WebSocket/SSE connection to the gateway (reporting `online`).
When a job arrives, the waker attempts to spawn the worker script (`--exec`) and redirect stdout/stderr to `~/.mco/logs/<instance>.log`.
Windows denies the file open request (`PermissionError: [Errno 13]` or `The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process`).
The worker executor exits with code 1 immediately without ever claiming or leasing the job.
How to Diagnose:
Inspect the waker log:
Get-Content ~\.mco\logs\BitCadence-wake-<role>-<instance>.log -Tail 30

Test whether the log file is locked:
[IO.File]::Open("$env:USERPROFILE\.mco\logs\<instance>.log", "Open", "Write", "None").Close()

If this throws an IOException, the file is locked by a lingering process.
How to Fix:
Find and terminate orphaned processes holding the lock:
Get-Process -Name python, pythonw, powershell | Where-Object { $_.Path -like "*BitCadence*" }

Kill the zombie process:
Stop-Process -Id <PID> -Force

Restart the waker service:
mco service restart BitCadence-wake-<role>-<instance>

title: Incident 2: Duplicate Wake Processes Competing for Jobs
text:
Incident 2: Duplicate Wake Processes Competing for Jobs
The Symptom:
When a single job is posted, two different instances attempt to process it simultaneously. You observe:
HTTP `409 Conflict` lease errors in logs.
Two git worktree folders created for the same job.
Git merge collisions (`index.lock` errors) in the repository.
Alternating heartbeats in `mco agents` with flickering process IDs.
The Root Cause:
A waker was registered in multiple supervisors at the same time:
Installed as a Windows Scheduled Task or systemd service via `mco service install-waker ROLE --exec COMMAND` or `mco fleet apply`.
Simultaneously started manually in a PowerShell terminal via `mco wake` or `mco listen`, OR launched by the Desktop Control Manager (`desktop.pyw`).
Both processes receive the SSE notification simultaneously and race to lease the job.
How to Diagnose:
Search all running processes for duplicate wakers:
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*mco.cli wake*" } | Select-Object ProcessId, CommandLine

Inspect active Task Scheduler tasks:
schtasks /query /fo LIST /v | Select-String "TaskName:.*BitCadence-wake"

How to Fix:
Terminate all duplicate instances:
Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*mco.cli wake*" } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }

Decide on a single supervision method:
**Either** use the Windows Desktop Control Manager (`scripts/desktop.pyw --start-all`), which automatically handles single-instance deduplication and Job Object cleanup.
**Or** use OS Task Scheduler via `mco fleet apply`. If using the Desktop Control Manager, click **Move workers into app** to disable redundant Task Scheduler entries.
Verify that exactly one waker process is running per configured worker.

title: Standing Score grants (local authority store)
text:
Standing Score grants (local authority store)
An operator can approve a reusable Score class once, then start runs from that
class without issuing another run grant. A class is the **exact canonical Score
digest**: constraints, budget, capabilities, resources, instructions, checkpoints,
and commit configuration are all bound. A different run ID is allowed; any change
to the Score needs a fresh approval. There are no wildcard classes.
Use the existing interactive Windows local-human approval boundary with
`MCO_LOCAL_HUMAN_GRANTS=true` and a configured Score signing key. Agent bearer
tokens and noninteractive terminals cannot issue or revoke local standing grants.
mco score grant-standing-local examples/scores/score-human-gate-canary.score.json --expires-hours 24
# Inspect the displayed policy and type the exact confirmation phrase once.
# Keep the returned grant ID for unattended start commands.
mco score start examples/scores/score-human-gate-canary.score.json --run-id class-run-001 --standing-grant GRANT_ID --target score-canary-worker=builder --target score-canary-review=reviewer
mco score tick --run-id class-run-001 --watch

# One command, no second confirmation phrase:
mco score revoke-standing-local GRANT_ID

Replace `GRANT_ID` with the issued ID and `builder`/`reviewer` with registered
instances for the example's worker/review roles. The example deliberately keeps
an explicit human checkpoint to demonstrate that standing authority preserves it.
Keep the existing conductor sweep for recurring progression. No new daemon or
scheduled process is installed. `--live-repository-write` is still required on
every tick for a repository-write Score. Existing independent review, branch
denylist, allowed-path restrictions, resource locks, evidence checks and human
checkpoints still apply. Standing grants never approve checkpoint decisions.
Standing authority is restricted to `repository:read`, `repository:write`,
`evidence:write`, `evidence:review`, and `cloud:inspect`, and to `test`, `development`,
or `staging` environments. Unknown capabilities are refused. Spending, public
publishing and production deployment are outside standing authority and require
separate human approval. Capability names describe the enforced adapter contract;
untrusted worker text cannot grant authority.
The budget ceiling is per run and bound by the Score digest. It is not a money
movement authorization or an aggregate spending allowance. The current local
bridge continues to refuse paid execution. Expiry is mandatory, at most 316 hours,
with a default of 24 hours. Both not-before and expiry are checked at use time.
Run startup with `--standing-grant` checks the exact class before creating the run.
The selected grant ID is stored with the run; every plan, dispatch (including
each job submission), and poll checks it again, including after process restart.
The authority service also checks the current source grant on every adapter use.
Revocation blocks future checks, including for previously started runs. Already
running commands are not cancelled; an effect that has passed its authority check
may finish. A blocked conductor run is not automatically resumed by a new grant.
New runs select the newest approval of an identical class. Every run is pinned
to its original source grant in the authority store on first successful use;
later approvals cannot revive a run whose original authority was revoked. A
revoked newest approval never falls back to older authority for a new run. A
separately approved, explicit run grant retains precedence and its own scope;
start such a run without `--standing-grant`. Standing-derived run grants are
ephemeral and cannot be copied into the durable run-grant table.
The local store lazily creates append-only `score_standing_grants`,
`score_standing_revocations`, `score_standing_runs`, and `score_standing_events` tables. Signed approvals
and revocations persist independently of conductor databases. Audit events cover
issuance, authorization, denial, and revocation, with grant/run/digest bindings,
timestamps, principal, and requested action/resource/environment/cost. Approval
and revocation records commit atomically with their audit event; audit write
failures prevent authorization from succeeding. Store write access is a trusted
boundary, as with existing run grants. The global STOP switch prevents standing
issuance and use; revocation remains available and never clears STOP.
This release supports the local SQLite authority store only. Remote authority
stores keep the existing explicit run-grant flow; no cloud schema or endpoint is
changed.

title: BitCadence interface review
text:
BitCadence interface review
Reviewed November 13, 2026. Lens: clear language, consistent meanings, details when needed, reliable feedback, and deliberate reversible actions. Findings below come from static source and routing inspection of clean main `0f9f36e` plus the existing shared checkout. They are not claims that a browser interaction or production failure was reproduced. No gateway, worker, token, schedule, job, approval or GPU state was changed.

title: Highest-value changes
text:
Highest-value changes
Fix misleading stop/approval feedback and cancellation behavior first. Then make administrative functions discoverable without forcing users to learn two partially overlapping web apps. The current everyday surfaces already have useful foundations: Ask previews before starting, helper repair diagnoses before confirmation, card states use words plus shapes, and Context promotion explains its future effect. Extend those patterns consistently rather than adding another flow builder or control panel.

title: Verified static findings
text:
Verified static findings
Source paths are repository-relative. Long UUID source filenames are mapped at the end. Priority indicates user impact, not a release approval.
ID / priority
Evidence and practical impact
Concrete simpler proposal
Acceptance check
U01 / P1
`ops.js:1020–1039` says Pause lets in-progress jobs finish. Its handler writes `MCO_KILL_SWITCH`; `admin_routes.py:413–458` calls `set_paused`, and `leases.py:241–255` marks renewable jobs halted and increments lease epoch. The same screen's advanced copy says active work halts. A person cannot predict what Pause will do.
Label it **Stop work**, explain **Halts active attempts and pauses new work. Resume permits new work; halted jobs need Retry.** Keep backend governance unchanged. Use a deliberate confirm summary for the existing effect; retain a fast emergency path where required.
Assert displayed explanation matches halt behavior in an isolated test; Resume never implies halted work auto-resumes.
U02 / P1
`dashboard.py:421–432`: `prompt(...)

'Aborted by operator'` submits an abort even when the user cancels. `:361–395` batch Cancel and `:526–530` individual Reject similarly convert prompt Cancel to an empty reason and continue.
U03 / P1
Console adapter `adapter.js:304–319` renders `res.success_count` and `res.failure_count`, but `routes.py:1670–1677` returns `succeeded` and `failed`. Batch feedback can say undefined succeeded/failed and mark partial failure as success. Selections are then cleared.
Derive counts from `succeeded.length` and `Object.keys(failed).length`; retain failed selections and a durable per-item result panel.
A controlled one-success/one-failure response shows accurate counts, reasons and retry scope.
U04 / P1
Clean-main `jobs.js:505–596` offers Reassign on active jobs, while the backend accepts unsuccessful terminal work. Clean `adapter.js:285–297` uses `to_role`/`to_instance` rather than required target fields. The shared dirty checkout repairs individual UI/body; that is pending work, not deployed proof. Batch UI still sends `to_role` (`jobs.js:385`) and adapter forwards it verbatim.
Integrate the existing individual repair through review; make batch use `target_agent_role`, state eligibility and replacement semantics. Keep live cancellation separate.
Failed/rejected/cancelled/halted can request a replacement; active/completed cannot. Single and batch body keys match schema and results show replacement identity.
U05 / P1
`pages.js:820–825` renders every non-rejected Recent decision with completed status, even if the approved job is waiting/running. This turns approval into false delivery evidence.
Show **Approved** as decision and actual job state separately.
An approved pending job reads Approved / Waiting, never Completed.
U06 / P1
`adapter.js:70–80` maps every HTTP 403 in `plainFailure` to “Your account isn't an approver yet” and `bitcadence fix`. This helper is used by batch and other operations. Scope, tenant or policy denial can receive an irrelevant privilege-repair instruction.
Preserve a typed server denial; distinguish missing scope, approver authority, tenant boundary and policy. Link to operator-admin instructions, not automatic privilege elevation.
Representative 403s retain their true reason and do not recommend unauthorized authority changes.
U07 / P1
`ops.js:535–547,595` says timezone comes from “your computer,” but Save sends no zone. `schedules_routes.py:48` defaults to `schedules_plain.detect_timezone()` on gateway host (`schedules_plain.py:73–89`). Remote browsers can create schedules at the wrong local time. Fixed-offset fallback can also ignore future DST.
Show **Time zone: [explicit IANA zone]** next to time and next occurrence. Send selected zone, validate it, and show the next occurrence including offset/date before save.
Browser and gateway in different zones produce the selected zone; next-run checks span a DST change.
U08 / P1
`desktop/app.py:77` directly calls `take_control`. `controller.py:153–161` disables scheduled tasks, stops all and restarts. UI label **Move workers into app** does not expose the process interruption or scheduled-task changes. **Stop all** also disables tasks and stops exact matching external workers (`controller.py:228–276`), while Exit only closes owned processes.
Add a review sheet listing affected components/tasks and current work, then **Move and restart workers**. Clarify Stop all vs Exit scopes beside the actions. Keep duplicate-start guard and ownership boundaries.
Read-only review sends no stop/task writes; confirmed handoff lists exact scope and preserves current ownership rules.
U09 / P2
Clean `shell.js:127` routes plain-tone Helpers without considering Advanced; token administration requires expert copy tone, available only through host prototype tweaks. Shared checkout introduces a pending Advanced/Manage fleet tokens doorway.
Expose a visible **Manage credentials…** disclosure from Helpers, with explicit admin scope, no design-mode dependency. Reuse the pending doorway after review.
Starting in default plain mode, an authorized user reaches token administration and returns without changing copy tone or unrelated preferences.
U10 / P2
`shell.js:203–216` has global Advanced; plain Settings nests another **Show advanced** disclosure (`ops.js:1049–1054`). A user must open technical detail to connect at all. The controls have different scope under the same word.
Put initial Connect setup directly in the disconnected empty state. Rename global toggle **Technical details**, local disclosure **Server administration**; retain the same permission checks.
First-time user can connect from empty state without searching for hidden fields; toggles describe what they reveal.
U11 / P2
`/console` has twelve pages; `/dashboard` has five overlapping pages and unique model connections, scoped agent editing, full settings and conductor controls (`dashboard.py:121–125`; `shell.js:4–17`). Current overview docs describe dashboard as merely “smaller, plainer.”
Make `/console` the clear everyday entry. Add one **Administration** doorway containing advanced capabilities with shared terminology/component patterns. Until merged, document dashboard's full scope and cross-link it.
Every unique action has one discoverable authoritative doorway; no feature is silently lost in consolidation.
U12 / P2
`ui.js:144–158` Drawer has no dialog role, label, Escape handling, focus trap or restoration. Job rows (`jobs.js:446`) and sortable `<th>` (`:402–439`) are mouse-click targets without key handlers. Approval queue nests checkbox inputs inside buttons (`pages.js:767–774`). Several inputs have placeholders/div text without associated labels.
Use accessible dialog primitives, native links/buttons inside cells, labelled controls and valid selectable-list markup. Keep sort dropdown as an alternative; add current-sort semantics.
Keyboard-only open/close/operate/return focus on each drawer; screen-reader names/states; valid interactive nesting. Static absence is verified; assistive-tech experience still needs runtime tests.
U13 / P2
Sidebar is fixed 216px with 12 controls of minimum 48px, sticky `height:100vh` and no own scrolling (`shell.js:138–190`). Content padding and several minimum grid widths consume small screens. Responsive sidebar rules are embedded only in mounted Home/Score and Ask styles (`pages.js:631`, `ask.js:34`), so navigation can change geometry across pages.
Collapsible navigation on narrow widths, independently scrollable sidebar for short screens, and single-column forms/details.
At 320px width and short-height/200% zoom, every nav item and primary action remains reachable without horizontal page travel. Actual overflow needs browser verification.
U14 / P2
`ui.js:160–188` removes toasts after 4.2 seconds, has no status/alert semantics, truncates bodies to one line, and offers no durable details. Several job handlers close editors without awaiting mutation success (`jobs.js:549,584,600`).
Await results, disable duplicate submit, keep errors beside the input, and retain an accessible result record linked to History. Do not close an unsuccessful form.
Controlled rejection stays visible and retains values; announcements are available; no double-submission while pending.
U15 / P2
JobBoard retains a selected-ID set while filters change (`jobs.js:225–303`); toolbar counts eligible jobs but several requests send all selected IDs (`:298–320`). Hidden selection and mixed eligibility undermine batch predictability.
Clear selection on scope changes or visibly show **N selected, M hidden**. Before action show exact eligible count and skipped count; retain failures after response.
Filtering a selected set never silently authorizes hidden work. Mixed-state batch describes all outcomes.
U16 / P2
`ops.js:1074–1091` renders every non-bool Gateway control as a text input even for choice metadata such as default sort. `/dashboard` already honors choice fields (`dashboard.py:831–841`).
Share the metadata renderer: switch, dropdown, labelled text or secret with field help.
Only allowed values are offered for choices; errors identify the actual field and retain unsaved values.
U17 / P2
Console Connector Test uses saved settings (`ops.js:722`), while fields remain editable and Save is separate. A green test can coexist with unsaved form changes; Sync appears after test success and can create work (`:774`).
Show dirty state and **Save and test**; invalidate prior success when relevant fields change. Label sync **Import now** with a preview/count where backend supports it.
Unsaved credentials cannot appear successfully tested; save/test/sync outcomes are distinct and tied to a settings revision.
U18 / P2
Governance copy promises “PDF cover page plus JSON” (`pages.js:935`) while export handler creates a single JSON blob (`:862–874`).
Call it **Download evidence JSON** and offer separate extract/download controls for returned file entries. Avoid implying legal certification.
Download labels and resulting filenames/types match exactly; bounded count/date coverage is visible.
U19 / P2
Job Board takes the shared 200-job window (`adapter.js:98`), Activity fetch caps at 500 (`jobs.js:927`), Context at 25 (`pages.js:1124`), Projects at 5,000 (`adapter.js:34`). Home/Projects expose limits, but “All work” and “Every step every agent took” overstate completeness.
Display **Showing latest N** and searched date/range consistently. Offer real server pagination/filtering rather than silently treating client filters as global search.
Missing older items never produce an unqualified “nothing found”; every count states its window.
U20 / P2
Connect AI filesystem actions are performed by gateway-side implementation; UI says apps “on this computer” and offers one-tap configuration (`ops.js:414–496`). A remote browser can interpret that as its own machine.
Show **Apps on [gateway host]** and a clear local/remote setup distinction. Only offer local installer-like claims for a local gateway.
A remote session names the target host before changes; client-side app discovery is not implied.
U21 / P3
Sidebar Jobs/Approvals/Helpers/Activity names differ from plain page titles (All work/Needs your OK/Your helpers/What happened), `shell.js:71–73,162`. Project docs say Uncategorized while source says Unassigned work.
Use one noun per destination in nav, headings, links and search aliases; preserve older names only as aliases.
Search for either historical name finds the one canonical guide and current control name.
U22 / P3
Existing `jev-routing.md:18–25` claims Settings → LLM Connections / Routing and sample model/confidence output, but neither routed GUI contains that task-routing form. `Overview`, `AutonomyControlCard`, `DemoLaunchPanel` and live-look components remain defined in `pages.js` but only Home is routed (`shell.js:121`).
Replace imaginary GUI steps with verified CLI instructions. Mark unreachable components as legacy/internal; remove obsolete guidance and screenshots after source owner review.
Every documented button has a reachable route and source reference; no mockup is presented as an implemented workflow.
U23 / P3
Desktop row actions silently return without selection (`desktop/app.py:117–120`), operate only on `selection()[0]`, yet Tk table permits multiple selection by default (`:60`). Reload settings can stop changed/removed workers (`controller.py:163–186`) despite sounding read-only.
Use single-row selection or implement explicit multi-row semantics; disable actions until selected. Label reload **Apply fleet changes…** and show affected workers before mutation.
Selection/action scope is unambiguous; applying config never surprises the user by stopping an undisclosed worker.
U24 / P3
Source paths and technical state locations appear in dashboard Live Look, while basic console has nested routes and some capabilities only in a second URL. Docs often expose long manual command/path workarounds for everyday actions.
Put operational effect and named host first, provide **Copy diagnostic details** disclosure for paths/IDs; make docs task-based with direct doorway links and recovery. Keep exact paths available for support.
A first-time operator identifies what is waiting and chooses the next action without reading a UUID/path; an expert can still copy exact evidence.

Apple guidance used for the review
[Design principles](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/design-principles/): keep meanings and interactions consistent, with useful feedback and room for character.
[Layout](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout): use progressive disclosure to keep common work easy to find.

title: Workers & Background Daemon Listening
text: Workers & Background Daemon Listening

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Connect external AI models (Anthropic Claude Desktop, OpenAI Codex, Google Antigravity, local scripts) to BitCadence dropboxes using the `mco listen` polling daemon, event wake triggers, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. The Worker Model
text:
1. The Worker Model
Helpers in BitCadence do not expose exposed HTTP endpoints or wait for inbound RPC calls. Instead, workers **poll their designated dropboxes** for mail:
A job arrives for role `codex`.
A running worker requests a lease atomically (`mco_lease` / `POST /api/jobs/lease_next`).
If won, the worker executes the task, streams events, and writes results back.

title: 2. Spawning a Background Listener
text:
2. Spawning a Background Listener
To start a worker daemon that polls for jobs:
# 1. Register the helper
mco register --name worker-codex-1 --role codex

# 2. Export the minted token
$env:MCO_AGENT_TOKEN = "mco_tok_..."

# 3. Start the polling daemon
mco listen --role codex --instance worker-codex-1

The daemon runs continuously, emitting log lines whenever work is checked, claimed, or completed.

title: 3. Event-Driven Wake (mco wake)
text:
3. Event-Driven Wake (`mco wake`)
If you prefer not to have a persistent polling process consuming memory:
Use `mco wake` to spawn your worker script only when pending work arrives in the mailbox:
mco wake --role codex --exec "python run_worker.py"

title: 4. Connecting via MCP (Model Context Protocol)
What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Automatic Lease Collision Avoidance:** If three workers run `mco listen` simultaneously for the same role, exactly one worker wins each task lease. The others receive empty responses and sleep until the next poll cycle.
**Lease Heartbeat Renewal:** Long-running jobs automatically send renewal heartbeats to prevent the gateway lease reaper from reclaiming the task prematurely.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Worker loop exits with 401 Unauthorized"
text:
1. "Worker loop exits with 401 Unauthorized"
**Cause:** `MCO_AGENT_TOKEN` is missing, expired, or invalid.
**Fix:** Verify the token using `mco status` and ensure the variable is set in the worker's session.

title: 2. "Worker claims job but crashes during execution"
text:
2. "Worker claims job but crashes during execution"
**Cause:** Unhandled exception in worker code.
**Fix:** The gateway lease reaper detects expired leases after the TTL (default: 5 minutes) and automatically resets the job status to `pending` (if retries remain) or routes it to the designated `escalate_to_role`.

title: Workflow Files
text: Workflow Files

title: Goal
text:
Goal
Run a multi-step pipeline from a saved YAML workflow file, with each step waiting for the one before it. For most work you don't need a file: say what you want on the **Ask for something** page and approve the plan it draws. See [Ask](Ask.md).
The drag-and-drop workflow builder and the Flow Control page (`/flow`) were removed from the console. **Ask for something** replaced them, and **Home** shows what is running. A workflow file is still the right tool when you want to keep a pipeline in version control and re-run it.

title: Step-by-Step Instructions
text: Step-by-Step Instructions

title: 1. The easy way: Ask
text:
1. The easy way: Ask
In the left menu, click **Ask for something**.
Type the request the way you'd tell a person, then click **Draft a plan**.
![Ask for something](img/21-console-ask.png)
Check the steps. Use **Remove a step**, **Always ask me at the end** or **Make it repeat** for light tweaks.
Click **Approve and start**. The steps appear on the job board as linked jobs, and **Home** shows them under **What's running**.

title: 2. Watching a pipeline
text:
2. Watching a pipeline
Click **Home**. Steps that wait on an earlier step show **Waiting**, a step that needs you shows **Needs you** with an **Approve** button, and a step that failed shows up under **What needs you**.
![Home](img/01-console-overview.png)

title: The CLI Equivalent
text:
The CLI Equivalent
A saved pipeline is a YAML file:
# pipeline.yaml
name: release-pipeline
steps:
  - id: research
    role: claude
    title: Research open bugs
    instructions: Identify critical bugs targeted for the v2.4 release.
  - id: fix
    role: codex
    title: Implement fixes
    instructions: Apply fixes identified in the research step.
    depends_on: [research]
  - id: ship
    role: codex
    title: Tag release
    instructions: Tag v2.4 release and publish artifacts.
    depends_on: [fix]
    requires_approval: true

Run the workflow:
mco workflow pipeline.yaml

title: What You'll See
text:
What You'll See
**Automatic Context Threading (Drumline):** When step 2 (`fix`) executes, BitCadence automatically prefixes its prompt with the **WORKFLOW THREAD** block containing the verbatim decisions and files from step 1 (`research`). No context is lost between different models.
**Automatic Gating:** When step 3 (`ship`) is reached, it automatically stops at `needs_approval` and waits for human sign-off.

title: If It Goes Wrong
text: If It Goes Wrong

title: 1. "Cyclic dependency detected"
text:
1. "Cyclic dependency detected"
**Cause:** Step A depends on Step B, and Step B depends on Step A.
**Fix:** Remove the circular reference in the YAML file. Workflows must be strict Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs).

title: 2. "Downstream steps fail after upstream failure"
text:
2. "Downstream steps fail after upstream failure"
**Cause:** By default, dependent steps remain `waiting` if an upstream parent fails.
**Fix:** Open the failed parent job, click **Retry**, or use `mco retry <parent-id>`. Once the parent succeeds, downstream steps unlock automatically.
